News.title: Bank tax would raise mortgage costs, warns UBS
News.content:
Bank stocks have fallen on fears that John Healey will launch a tax raid on the sector in the Budget.

NatWest and Lloyds Banking Group shares were both down more than 2pc in early trading on the London Stock Exchange as investors responded to news the Chancellor is poised to raise taxes on the industry.

The banking sector has come into Mr Healey’s focus after their earnings were boosted by higher interest rates caused by the Iran war.

He is understood to be planning to target lenders despite praising banks at an International Monetary Fund (IMF) event in Bangkok on Thursday.

He said: “They’re a big contributor to the economy.

“They’re an important part of our business. They’re a part of the jewel, if you like, in the British economic crown.” Here is what you need to know.

5 things to start your day

1) Healey poised to launch raid on banks | Chancellor prepares to target lenders despite playing down fears of higher levies in the Budget

2) UAE bid for Telegraph threatened press freedom, Ofcom found | Media watchdog concluded takeover by RedBird IMI was contrary to the public interest

3) John Lewis puts Snowdonia hotel up for sale | Retail group makes ‘tough decision’ to offload historic staff retreat amid high running costs

4) Britain prepares to hand military satellite contract to US defence giant | US move to curtail Ukraine’s access to Starlink triggers ‘kill switch’ fears around Lockheed Martin’s Skynet bid

5) Cult London cinema beloved by Tarantino saved from closure | The Prince Charles Cinema secures its future with 25-year lease after bitter landlord dispute

What happened overnight

Asian shares mostly rose a day after a tech sell-off dragged stocks lower.

South Korea’s benchmark Kospi index jumped 3.6pc, after tumbling 7.6pc on Thursday. Samsung Electronics was up 4.2pc, while memory chipmaker SK Hynix added 3.5pc.

Japan’s Nikkei 225 rose 1.9pc to 65,658.59, after falling 4.9pc a day earlier. OpenAI investor SoftBank climbed 1.7pc. Chip equipment maker Tokyo Electron was 2.8pc higher and memory chipmaker Kioxia advanced 3.2pc.

The Asian technology stocks traded higher after losses in AI shares moderated in the US.

Kevin Warsh, the chairman of the US Federal Reserve, said Friday at the IMF and World Bank gathering in ⁠Bangkok that AI could bring about positive impacts to global economies.

He said: “I’d say, the advent of this new technology is probably the most consequential change to the U.S. and the global economy in my lifetime.

“There really is, I think, a huge benefit to the global economy, the US economy, over the horizon.”

Taiwan’s Taiex, which also benefited from the AI frenzy, was up 0.6pc. But shares of TSMC, or Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Co, were 0.4pc lower even as it posted record quarterly profits on Thursday and said AI demand remained very strong.

In Indonesia, the Jakarta Composite index fell more than 10pc, the lowest in years, after MSCI said Indonesia’s continued classification as an emerging market would be “no longer appropriate.”

Hong Kong’s Hang Seng gained 1.2pc to 24,353.69. The Shanghai Composite index rose 1pc to 3,742.66.

Australia’s S&P/ASX 200 was 1.1pc higher at 8,812.90.

India’s Sensex edged up 0.2pc.

News.title: Are my smart home devices always watching me? How to stay safe (and private) in a connected house
News.content:
The past decade has seen a huge rise in the number of smart devices in the home, from video doorbells to robot vacuum cleaners.

Smart connectivity offers many useful upsides, from letting us keep an eye on package deliveries to streamlining household chores. However, concerns remain about whether these devices are safe from hackers and how they might impinge on our privacy.

As a technology journalist for almost 20 years, I have reviewed many smart appliances and have lots of connected devices in my own home, so I’m an experienced user. To find out more about their potential downsides, and how to keep yourself protected, I’ve also spoken to an expert from cybersecurity firm Kaspersky, a board member at the Connected Standards Alliance (CSA) – which promotes openness and safety within smart-device networks – as well as other leading brands in the space.

What is a smart appliance?

A smart appliance connects to your home network, often via Wi-Fi, to allow for a wider range of interactions. That might be a washing machine that notifies you when it’s finished, or a fridge-freezer such as the Samsung Family Hub with a screen and voice controls.

But smart appliances don’t have to be huge: connected lightbulbs, baby monitors, smart plugs and more can all link up with your home network, in many cases integrating with voice assistants such as Amazon’s Alexa or Apple’s Siri.

News.title: Pierre Sage’s Lyon return ends in disappointment for Crystal Palace
News.content:
Good evening and welcome to our live coverage of Thursday night’s European football with Crystal Palace, Sunderland and Bournemouth in Europa League action, and Brighton hosting Kauno Zalgiris in the Uefa Conference League.

Palace manager Pierre Sage managed Lyon between November 2023 and January 2025, and another sub-plot is American businessman John Textor’s involvement with the French club. The former Palace shareholder was the reason the club missed out on Europa League participation last season because Lyon were in the same competition and thus Palace were considered in breach of multi-club ownership rules. Textor sold his stake in Palace, but despite the club’s best efforts they had to settle for the Conference League, a competition they subsequently won.

Palace could have been three or four down against Nottingham Forest at the weekend but fought back for a much-needed Premier League victory. They made a winning start in Europe, beating Lech Poznan 4-0 at Selhurst Park in their opening Europa League game.

Bournemouth and Sunderland also made winning starts, despite both teams’ poor form domestically. Sunderland travel to Portuguese side Torreense, while Sturm Graz are the opposition for Bournemouth’s first ever European game at the Vitality Stadium (or Dean Court if you prefer). Bournemouth continue to be without Justin Kluivert, Eli Junior Kroupi and Alex Scott because of injury.

Brighton are favourites to win the Conference League and play their first game in the competition against Lithuanian club Kauno Zalgiris. Lifting the trophy in Istanbul at the end of the season would assure Brighton of a place in next season’s Europa League, though given their Premier League form and Manchester City’s predicament, Champions League qualification could be a realistic aspiration. Brighton won with 10 men at Sunderland on Saturday, and were successful in their appeal against Pascal Struijk’s red card.

Full team news on the way shortly.

News.title: Economy slows before Healey’s maiden Budget
News.content:
The Chancellor said banks are too often seen as “distant financial institutions”, in a sign he will not raise taxes on the industry in the Budget.

John Healey has faced pressure to impose a windfall tax on bank profits to help rebuild an expected decline in his wiggle room in the public finances.

John Healey said: “My observations on the banks are just that people too often see them as a big distant financial institutions when they are hardwired into the economic fabric of this country and our future prospects.

“That said, you know I’ve got decisions to take in the Budget, and I will. I’ll set those out in two weeks’ time.

“And my special responsibility as Chancellor is to protect the resilience of the British economy for the future. That the resilience that the IMF has reported on this week by upgrading our growth figures in the UK this week, that the welcome monthly growth figures published this morning reinforce, and importantly, alongside that, the IMF reports said that Britain stands out for our deficit reduction plans, and will have his forecast actually a reflection not just on forecast plans but performance over the last couple of years. You know, a consolidation plan in place and underway.

“I’ve said from day one and week one, and I’ve had Andy Burnham in lockstep alongside me, I will meet those fiscal rules in full.

“That will be part of the Budget that I set out in two weeks’ time, and I think the IMF report reinforces that that is not just a not just a reinforcing the strength of Britain’s position, but something that they say they want to see other countries doing as well.”

THE last great Leeds team is now 25 years ago. David O’Leary’s ‘babies’ finished third in the Prem before sweeping aside the likes of Barcelona and AC Milan on their way to the Champions League semi-finals.

Then chairman Peter Ridsdale started renting goldfish. It’s been a long road back.

And tomorrow at Elland Road, vastly improved this season under Daniel Farke, they have the biggest of all fish to fry – Man United.

There will be no sympathy for those Red Devils travelling across the Peninnes, just delight at the sight of their bitter rivals floundering on all fronts.





After rescuing them at Christmas last year and steering them back into the Champions League, Michael Carrick is finding himself where all Old Trafford bosses eventually end up.

Sooner rather than later if your first name is not Alex and your second one Ferguson: clear favourite in the Sack Race.

After the club’s worst start in 40 years, Carrick is now as short as 5-4 in places to be the next Prem boss to be axed.

His side are stranded in 13th, with one league win all season, and were done 2-0 at Atletico Madrid in Europe on Tuesday night.

And all that before Lisandro Martinez stuck his oar in and blamed the owners for the state of play. True in part it may be, helpful it wasn’t.

What Carrick needs, of course, is what Farke got – a board that stood behind him in times of trouble.

Less than a year ago, the Whites were in the drop zone and the German looked doomed.

Now they’re seventh and had champions Arsenal in big trouble at the Emirates last weekend before succumbing to their first defeat of the season.



Bet Balls Everton and Chelsea to draw 2-2 today is 9-1 with BetGoodwin

Brighton to beat Palace tomorrow and BTTS second half is 6-1 with BetGoodwin

Leeds to beat Man United 3-1 tomorrow is 12-1 with BetGoodwin

Arsenal to win at Forest tomorrow, BTTS is 13-5 with BetGoodwin GET £15 IN FREE BETS WITH BETGOODWIN

Tomorrow they will kick off as best-priced 7-5 favourites with Unibet, with the visitors 19-10 with Sporting Index and the draw trading at 14-5 with Betfair.

More than good value, says Coral’s Dave Stevens: “The good times are back at Elland Road, and the Premier League is all the better for it. Keep those levels up, and 4-1 about a top-six finish would look decent value.

“As for Man U, anyone backing them at 4-5 for a top-six finish needs a lie down! The 7-2 they finish in the bottom half has much more appeal.

“This is a proper heavyweight clash between two old enemies, Elland Road will be rocking, and I can only see one winner! Leeds should be odds-on in my book, so 7-5 about a home win looks a massive price.”

Agreed. Carrick’s side have beaten only the Azerbaijan champions Sabah in their last seven games, look all at sea at the back and will have to show something they haven’t to get anything tomorrow.



Leeds are organised, hard working, coherent – and rested. Home win BTTS is the selection at 3-1 with betfair, William Hill and Sky Bet. A 1-1 draw heads the correct-score market at 7-1 but 9-1 on a Leeds 2-1 win looks about right.

Dominic Calvert-Lewin is the 5-1 pick to open the scoring with Coral and Ladbrokes.

Dark horse

Goodwinners’ Enclosure

THREE points, three goals, no wins. Spurs flirting with relegation – it’s starting to look like a serious relationship!

While they showed plenty of fight to earn a late point at Man Utd on Saturday, and are out to 15-2 in our relegation book, our punters still continue to back them for the drop.

Behind Roberto De Zerbi’s under-the-cosh side in the betting, the three promoted sides are making a good fist of staying up.

But despite smashing Newcastle 4-1 on Monday night, Coventry remain our 4-9 favourites for the drop, with eighth-placed Hull 4-6 and 10th-placed Ipswich 19-10.

Man City though are now into 11-8 third-favoutites, with Fulham 19-10.



At least we’re talking about the Premier League again and we welcomed its return with open arms here at BetGoodwin Towers.

And champions Arsenal got proceedings back underway with a punter-friendly win over Leeds, but not without a scare at 1-0 down.

While we snagged a few quid back with that 1-1 draw at Old Trafford, we perhaps showed a bit too much love to our customers on Super Sunday – going City even money when Ryan Gravenberch got sent off at 0-0 for Liverpool at Anfield.

The punters piled in and Erling Haaland, inevitably getting on the scoresheet, and co did the rest, knocking off a comprehensive 3-0 win.

With Man Utd continuing to disappoint, the pressure is mounting on boss Michael Carrick.



Tuesday night’s defeat at Atletico and Lisandro Martinez’s big stir of the pot after are not the ideal build up ahead of tomorrow’s tricky test away at Leeds.

The Elland Road side are our favourites at 27-20 and rightly so, given their impressive form. However, at 7-4, United, who have a habit of turning it on when you least expect it, could be the value here.

Despite their ongoing frustrations, we’re gonna stick our necks out and say Man Utd win and BTTS at 10-3 is the best bet of the game.

Today’s early kick off sees Everton host Chelsea, with the Toffees boasting an impressive record at the Hill Dickinson.

And while the Blues were blistering at home in demolishing Bournemouth 5-1 last weekend, they have already lost twice on the road this term. At 21-10, Everton could prove to be an appealing option for punters looking to take advantage of Chelsea’s away day woes.



Finally, the BetGoodwin Banker Acca for this weekend is: Fulham, Norwich, Leicester and Barnet all to win at a boosted 11-1!

A NEW South Wales? If you had to pick a side to go up from the Principality this season, it probably wouldn’t have been Swansea.

Cardiff had been promoted from League One and FC Hollywood Wrexham had just missed out on the play-offs.

But two 11th-placed finishes in a row should have been a clue that the Swans knew their way around the division.

And 10 games in, Vitor Matos’ side are sitting pretty two points clear at the top.



Unbeaten at home (at the no taking Liberty Stadium) and only one defeat all season, their promotion credentials will be closely examined today by the pre-season title favourites when West Ham roll into town.

Nuno Espirito Santos boys certainly put the Hammer down in midweek, winning 6-0 at Lincoln, and will start 5-4 favourites with Betfred, with the home side 11-5 with Coral.

Brentford vs Liverpool preview

Brentford will hope to extend their unbeaten run when Liverpool visit this afternoon.

The Bees are unbeaten in their six Premier League games so far this season and, overall, have avoided defeat in eight top-flight matches – the longest current run of any side.

Keith Andrews’ side sit fourth in the division, although there’s a sense they perhaps should be higher given they’ve dropped eight points from winning positions this season.

They certainly didn’t make that mistake when cruising to a 3-0 victory over Chelsea in their last home outing and will hope to take another heavyweight scalp at the Gtech Community Stadium today.



It wouldn’t be a massive shock, either, given Brentford were unbeaten in their two Premier League games against Liverpool last season (W1 D1).

There’s also a nice bonus in knowing that Andoni Iraola’s lowest points-per-game return in the Premier League has come against Brentford. He’s picked up just two points in six games against the Bees as Bournemouth manager.

But that could be easier said than done against a Liverpool side who’ve won their last two away Premier League games, keeping a clean sheet in both.

Sports.title: Kai Rooney, 16, makes Man Utd U21s debut as he follows in footsteps of dad Wayne.. but first appearance ends in disaster
Sports.content:
Next

KAI ROONEY’s debut appearance for the Manchester United U21s ended in disaster.

The son of club legend Wayne was sent on as a substitute during the Premier League 2 fixture against Nottingham Forest.



Kai, 16, was subbed on in the 77th minute with the young Red Devils level with the Tricky Trees.

The youngster would have been hoping to have made the difference and marked his debut with a winning goal.



However, it did not work out like that as United lost 3-2 with Shakur Samuels netting the decisive goal for Forest.

Ahead of the match, Kai showed his excitement about the opportunity on Instagram.

He posted a picture of his kit hanging on the wall in the changing room with the caption: “U21s vs Forest.”

The chance handed to Kai follows on from his debut for the club’s U19s against Atletico Madrid in the Uefa Youth League.

That game also ended in defeat for United, with the Spaniards scoring three goals.

Kai has been promoted in the United youth teams after featuring for United’s Under-16s last season.



SUN VEGAS WELCOME OFFER: GET UP TO £100 BONUS

In July, he was handed a scholarship with the Red Devils – typically a full-time, two-year apprenticeship agreement with United’s academy.

SunSport revealed in February that the contract would switch to a three-year pro deal worth around £50,000 a year with an annual signing-on fee.

Kai is part of a talented batch of United youngsters which also includes Jacey Carrick – son of first-team manager Michael.

Father Wayne, 40, made his debut in the Premier League at the age of 16 as he emerged as a talent at Everton in 2002.



Two years later, he was snapped up by United in a £30million transfer and capped his debut with a hat-trick in the Champions League.

He went on to make 559 appearances for the club in all competitions and scored a club record 253 goals.

Sports.title: Regulators are right that football has massive problem with money – but clubs are much more than simply businesses
Sports.content:
Next

FOOTBALL has a financial problem. It may also be about to acquire a regulatory one.

The Independent Football Regulator’s ‘State of the Game’ report this week delivered a grim verdict on a £9billion industry.



Ninety-four per cent of clubs are losing money. Aggregate losses have reached £1.7billion.

More than a quarter of clubs could not survive a month if their owners stopped paying the bills.



The figures are alarming. But football has never been a business for the faint-hearted.

And the question is whether the regulator intends to make it safer, or simply less ambitious.



There was precious little financial security before the Premier League was born in 1992.

In the early 1980s, attendances collapsed, clubs struggled to pay the bills and some sold their grounds to local authorities to survive. A 1982 report found the 92 league clubs were collectively losing £6m a year.

Football did not emerge from that crisis by discovering the joys of financial caution. It reinvented itself. The Premier League broke away, secured its own broadcasting deals and built a commercial phenomenon. Average Prem club revenues have since grown more than 30-fold.

That is the inconvenient truth for anyone who believes football can be regulated into prosperity.



SUN VEGAS WELCOME OFFER: GET UP TO £100 BONUS

Its success was built by people prepared to take risks, invest money and imagine their club could be something greater than it was.

I sat through every Prem meeting on these issues and every House of Lords debate on the legislation.

And I understand why football needs proper safeguards. I also know how easily a well-intentioned intervention can have consequences its authors never anticipated.

This is why I have repeatedly warned in the House of Lords against treating football like a bank.

Financial resilience matters, but a football club is not simply a business seeking to minimise risk.



It exists to win promotion, avoid relegation and, occasionally, achieve something extraordinary.

If regulation makes every decision about survival rather than success, a football club that avoids risk may be condemned to mediocrity. Financial sustainability matters, but so does sporting jeopardy.

Promotion, relegation, ambition and the possibility of an unlikely triumph are not unfortunate side effects of football’s business model. They are the business model.



Nobody wants another Bury, another club disappearing while its supporters are left wondering how it happened.

Owners who spend money they do not have can do lasting damage to communities.

But a regulator that tries to eliminate every financial risk could eliminate much of the reason people invest in football in the first place.

There is a difference between stopping reckless spending and stopping clubs from spending. It is a difference the regulator will need to understand.

Take cash. The IFR is right to worry about clubs that cannot survive a month without fresh money from their owners. Bills do not accept promises and players cannot be paid in potential.



But cash is not the same as value. Football clubs own or control valuable assets: Players, stadiums, training grounds and commercial rights.

The IFR does consider squad values in its solvency analysis.

Yet the distinction between a club with a temporary cash-flow problem and one with an unsustainable business matters.

The recent valuation of Behdad Eghbali’s Chelsea at a massive £5bn shows the extraordinary capital value that football can generate. Assets are not cash and valuations can evaporate in the blink of an eye. But neither should financial health be reduced to a snapshot of the bank balance.

The real problem is that clubs are caught in a vicious circle.



Financial rewards for reaching the Prem are so vast, that Championship owners are tempted to spend beyond their means to get there.

Telling clubs to behave more cautiously does not remove that incentive. It tells them to compete with one hand tied behind their backs.

Meanwhile, the money is not always going where it should. The IFR says agents’ fees reached £484million in 2025-26.

Nearly half a billion pounds went to intermediaries, while clubs across the pyramid struggled to balance their books.

There is surely more scope to tackle waste here than in the ambition to build a better team.



Nor can the growing gap between the Prem and the EFL be ignored.

The top flight is the financial engine of English football, it funds the entire pyramid as it is.

More money flowing down the pyramid may be part of the answer. It cannot be the whole answer if it simply fuels higher wages, transfer fees and agent commission.

The regulator must also understand what it should not regulate.

Consider Manchester City. IFR chair David Kogan said decisions about whether owners are fit to run a club must be based on evidence and statutory tests, not diplomatic relationships.



He has pledged to resign if political interference compromises the regulator’s work. That independence is essential.

The Newcastle takeover provides a warning. In 2021, then-Prem chairman Gary Hoffman told clubs the Government had applied pressure over the approval of the Saudi-backed deal, while insisting that the pressure had not influenced the decision.

Hoffman announced his departure weeks later amid a backlash over the handling of the takeover.

Kogan must be free to assess City’s owners on the evidence, just as he must be free to reach a conclusion that ministers may dislike.

A regulator that can be swayed by political convenience is not independent.



One that uses its independence to expand its own reach without restraint is not necessarily wise.

In the House of Lords, I set out three tests for the regulator: Protect growth, remain light-touch and exercise independent judgement.

Those are not just concessions to football’s richest clubs. They are safeguards for the entire game.

The IFR’s report is a warning and it deserves to be taken seriously. But a warning is not a licence to treat every club as a problem to be managed, and every owner as a risk to be contained.

English football has never been free of financial danger.



Its success has come from taking risks, attracting investment and turning a domestic competition into a global business.

Now the challenge is to make that success more resilient, not regulate away the ambition that created it.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

The sun is shining on a £9bn industry. The regulator is right to ask what happens when it rains.

But it must not mistake carrying an umbrella for building a better football club.

Sports.title: Wayne Rooney's son Kai, 16, makes debut for Man Utd U21s but it doesn't go to plan
Sports.content:
Wayne Rooney's son Kai, 16, makes debut for Man Utd U21s but it doesn't go to plan

Kai Rooney came on for Manchester United's Under-21s against Nottingham Forest as a second-half substitute but couldn't prevent the young Red Devils falling to defeat

View 2 Images Rooney Jr made his bow for United's U21s (Image: Daniel Weir/Sports Press Photo/Shutterstock)

Wayne Rooney's 16-year-old son, Kai, made his debut for Manchester United's Under-21s on Friday night - but couldn't prevent them falling to defeat.

‌



‌



Rooney Jr came on as a 77th-minute substitute against Nottingham Forest in Premier League 2, his first taste of football at that level.

‌



The match at Loughborough University Stadium was tied at 2-2 when Rooney entered the fray, but just a couple of minutes later Forest took the lead and went on to claim all three points.

‌



Kai is the same age as dad Wayne was when he spectacularly announced himself in the Premier League with a screamer for Everton against Arsenal coining the famous commentary line: "Remember the name."

‌



And England icon Rooney's son has now taken another step towards playing for United's first team, something which seems inevitable in the coming years.

Kai's first appearance for the U21s comes after his bow in the UEFA Youth League for United's U19s against Atletico Madrid, a game which also ended in defeat.

He has been promoted through the youth ranks having starred for United's U16s last term. He posted on Instagram before his bow for the U21s with a picture of his kit hanging in the dressing room, captioning: "U21s vs Forest."

‌



Kai signed a two-year apprenticeship in United's academy in July which will switch to a three-year professional deal worth around £50,000 a year. United manager Michael Carrick's son, Jacey, is also in United's youth ranks.

View 2 Images Kai Rooney with his parents after winning the Premier League Shield (Image: Instagram/@waynerooney)

Fuad Ayorinde Smith pounced to fire Forest ahead in the youth clash before United skipper Dan Armer levelled from the penalty spot.

Article continues below

United then went in front through Samuel Lusale but Forest equalised as Smith converted a penalty of his own. Forest substitute Shakur Samuels scored the winner.

Rooney Sr was signed by United for £30million in 2004 and scored a hat-trick on his debut in the Champions League. He would go on to score a club record 253 goals in 559 appearances, winning five Premier League titles along the way.

Sports.title: Man City charges LIVE: Points deduction size emerges as Premier League rivals 'fuming'
Sports.content:
All of the latest Manchester City 114 charges news with updates on their potential points deduction and the reaction of Premier League rivals

Hello and welcome to Mirror Football's live blog on the Manchester City charges case...

Last month, the Premier League confirmed an independent commission found City guilty of 114 financial breaches but the process still has a long way to run. City have appealed the decision and a final outcome this season is seen as unlikely even though a sanctions hearing is also set to take place.

Discussed at that will be all the potential punishments, ranging from a hefty fine to expulsion from the Premier League, with City warned they could face 'multiple double figure' points deductions.

The process being drawn out has already angered other top-flight clubs with many of the belief it is impacting their ability to qualify for the Champions League while others are more concerned about potential legal costs.

With all of that being said, stay with us throughout the day for the latest news and updates on the Man City charges case!

Sports.title: Liverpool news: Andoni Iraola draws closer to £100m star as he's sent 'overspent' message
Sports.content:
Liverpool news: Andoni Iraola draws closer to £100m star as he's sent 'overspent' message

Liverpool's latest round-up includes an update on a key target

View 2 Images Andoni Iraola could be busy in January (Image: Robbie Jay Barratt - AMA, Getty Images)

Avoiding back-to-back Premier League defeats will be Liverpool's sole mission this weekend. The Reds are coming off a 3-0 loss at home to Manchester City last week, but followed that up with a comprehensive 6-3 win over LASK in the Champions League.

‌



‌



As is the case most weeks in the top flight, there's rarely a fixture that doesn't come with many difficulties, and the Reds' Saturday afternoon clash against Brentford possesses just that. Keith Andrews' side sit fourth in the table and are one of just three teams that remain unbeaten in the opening six games of the season.

‌



The match at the Gtech Community Stadium will provide another stern test for Andoni Iraola's Reds. The Spaniard is slowly approaching his first January transfer window at Liverpool, which could see him reunite with Bournemouth's Alex Scott following the latest update on the midfielder's future.

‌



Meanwhile, Iraola has been told he'll follow in Arne Slot's footsteps this season by a former Reds star. Mirror Football delves into the latest stories coming out of Anfield...

Reds in 'driving seat' for Scott

Liverpool are reportedly leading the race to sign Scott in January, which would see the 23-year-old join forces with Iraola once again. News emerged earlier this week that Bournemouth are willing to sanction a sale for their prized asset, but would seek a bid of £100million for his services.

The Reds showed interest in the England star, who played under Iraola for the Cherries, this past summer. He was the subject of an intense pursuit from Chelsea, with Xabi Alonso's side tabling several offers for Scott, the highest bid being £68m.

‌



However, the Mail reports that the Reds are now in the "driving seat" for Scott's signature. It remains to be seen whether Liverpool's hierarchy will trigger yet another £100m+ signing, given the midfielder has 20 months left on his contract.

View 2 Images Alex Scott could be on his way out of Bournemouth in January (Image: Getty Images)

‌



Iraola told he'll fail like Slot

A successful and realistic debut season for Iraola at Liverpool, for many fans, would be a top-four finish and a deep cup run. However, even that is a step too far to achieve, according to former Reds star Dietmar Hamann.

He claimed the Spaniard would fail to lead the club to the top four like Arne Slot last season. The ex-Germany international said: "Finishing in the top four for Liverpool this season will be a success, but I don’t see it happening," he said. "I don't see closing that 25-point gap with Arsenal from last year."

Hamann, 53, said his former side face too much competition in their fight for Champions League qualification. He added: "This season they've got a fight on their hands to finish in the top four.

‌

Then I expect Man United to turn things around at some stage, depending on what happens with the manager."

Hamann also took aim at Liverpool's spending over the past year, which has included over £300m spent just on Florian Wirtz, Alexander Isak and Bradley Barcola. The 2005 Champions League winner added: "Liverpool's only chance is Iraola getting a tune out of those players brought in last year but so far he hasn’t managed it.

Sports.content:
Man Utd news: 'Ridiculous' JJ Gabriel plan slammed as star punished by club

Manchester United have endured a nightmare few weeks both on and off the field and things are showing no signs of improving

View 2 Images JJ Gabriel's future has yet to be resolved (Image: Manchester United via Getty Images)

The pressure has been mounting on Manchester United and their manager Michael Carrick after another defeat in midweek. The Red Devils have now gone more than a month without a win in any competition and face a tough trip to Leeds United on Sunday afternoon.

‌



‌



United's frustrations have spilt over into off-field matters as well. Talented academy star JJ Gabriel looks poised to leave the club before playing a senior competitive minute after frustrations at a lack of action this term.

‌



Carrick's team sit 13th heading into this weekend's action, three points and six places behind their opponents. If other results go the way of struggling teams on Saturday, United could be looking over their shoulders by the time they kick off at Elland Road.

‌



As we head into a potentially pivotal weekend, there has also been further fallout from the frustrating Champions League loss against Atletico Madrid on Tuesday. Here are our latest likes from around Old Trafford.

FOLLOW OUR MAN UTD FB PAGE! Latest United news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

Lisandro Martinez wants to LEAVE Man Utd as reason for bombshell rant becomes clear READ MORE :

Man Utd ROCK BOTTOM in Europe as five-year transfer splurge completely exposed READ MORE :

Gabriel plan slammed

Former Everton chief executive Keith Wyness has been left baffled by suggestions Manchester United might take legal action over JJ Gabriel's desire to leave. The teenager requested the club cancel his registration - something United have seemingly been unwilling to do - but a move to the continent still looks more likely than not.

‌



"I think it's about a 30 per cent chance of him staying put and 70 per cent going to Real Madrid. I think it's that far in their favour," Wyness told Football Insider

"I think too much has been said and too much has gone under the bridge. Man United either didn't act appropriately; probably last year was the time to do it. They obviously haven't made the window for his success, his match plan and his pathway very clear to him."

He added: "I've had countless young players come through, and I've seen each of them develop in different ways. United are now talking about going legal. I mean, that's ridiculous, and I think it would be the wrong way to go."

‌



Martinez learns his punishment

View 2 Images Lisandro Martinez was not happy after Manchester United's defeat against Atletico Madrid (Image: Manchester United via Getty Images)

United have slapped Lisandro Martinez with a fine following his outburst in the aftermath of Tuesday's defeat in Spain, according to BBC Sport. The centre-back launched into a tirade in which he appeared to indicate the club's summer business left them ill-equipped to kick on after qualifying for the Champions League.

Martinez, for his part, has issued an apology for his words. "Today I met with the club's leadership and the manager. It was a very positive conversation, where we were able to exchange views and speak openly about what happened after Tuesday's game," the Argentina international wrote on social media.

Article continues below

"Everyone knows that I am a passionate person and that I live football with great intensity. The frustration of the defeat led me to express how I felt at a time and place that perhaps were not the right ones, and for that I want to apologise."

A new series from Jack Thorne, the acclaimed writer of Adolescence, will focus on Bill Shankly's reign as Liverpool manager which saw the Reds go from the old Second Division to being champions of England

View 2 Images Jude Law will play the iconic manager (Image: Patrick T. Fallon/AFP)

Jude Law is set to play legendary former Liverpool manager Bill Shankly in a new TV series. Written by Jack Thorne of Adolescence fame, the show will be focus on Shankly's success at Anfield, as he transformed Liverpool into a global footballing powerhouse.

‌



‌



Liverpool chairman Tom Werner believes that the series could become like The Crown and follow the club beyond Shankly's reign further seasons. Under the Scot - who passed away in 1981 - Liverpool were promoted from the old Second Division and would go on to win three First Division titles, two FA Cups, four Charity Shields and one UEFA Cup in his 15-year reign on Merseyside.

‌



Werner told Deadline, who broke the news of Law's casting: "It's a story about family and relationships through the lens of a football club. My feeling is, if you do nothing more in that first episode than show 50,000 people singing You'll Never Walk Alone, I defy anyone who won't be moved by that one scene."

‌



Law, who is a BAFTA winner and two-time Oscar nominee, supports one of Liverpool's Premier League rivals, Tottenham. The 53-year-old is also a fan of cricket.

‌



Shankly's granddaughter, Karen Gill, is involved alongside production company Box To Box Films. Filming will take place in Liverpool and at Anfield, giving the series an authentic feel.

Gill commented: "I think it's a wonderful way to share the story of my grandad's time at LFC. Anybody who knows anything about the club knows what it meant to Bill Shankly.

"This is going to be a must watch for all Liverpool fans and it's a privilege to have the chance now to showcase his story to the wider world. I'm looking forward to seeing how this project unfolds and being a part of it."

‌



Where will Liverpool finish this season? Give us your prediction in the comments section.

View 2 Images Bill Shankly had a profound impact on the city of Liverpool (Image: Central Press/Getty Images)

Thorne added: "I'm excited to be telling this incredible story and it's an honour to be working alongside A24 and Liverpool Football Club. Our goal is to focus not just on the club, but on the city itself - because, and this is one thing Bill Shankly made sure, the club belongs to the city and the city belongs to the club.

Article continues below

"We have a chance with this show to celebrate both a magnificent football club and a magnificent city, whilst being honest about the struggles of the 1960s and 1970s in one of our industrial heartlands. We hope to honour the fans, to the city, and the legacy of Liverpool FC in bringing its story to life."

Sports.title: Mikel Arteta sets Noni Madueke and Viktor Gyokeres challenges amid Arsenal exit talk
Sports.content:
Mikel Arteta sets Noni Madueke and Viktor Gyokeres challenges amid Arsenal exit talk

Noni Madueke and Viktor Gyokeres have struggled to to find consistent form since joining Arsenal from Chelsea and Sporting Lisbon respectively and both have been linked with moves away

View 3 Images Noni Madueke and Viktor Gyokeres have endured tricky form at Arsenal (Image: Getty Images)

Mikel Arteta has backed Noni Madueke to show his real quality and deliver for Arsenal when they need him most. Madueke, 24, has been hit-and-miss since joining Arsenal in a huge £52m move from Chelsea in the summer of 2025.

‌



‌



England winger Madueke has struggled to hold down a regular place at the Emirates amid competition from Bukayo Saka, Eberechi Eze and now Christos Tzolis. Madueke has also lost his England place after being dropped for the first squad since the World Cup as he tries to rediscover his form.

‌



But Arteta says that Madueke now has a big opportunity in the next few weeks with Tzolis out injured and he believes the former Chelsea winger will take his chance. Gunners boss Arteta said: “If we give the possibility to any player to give him two or three or four games in a row, I think everybody will appreciate that because they will get more familiar with the players, more minutes, more confidence.

‌



“If things go well, that is the ideal thing to do with all of them. He had a few and he will have more minutes in the next few games. I am sure that we will start to see a closer version of Noni at the highest level.”

Make sure you don't miss sport's biggest stories and breaking news by making the Daily Mirror one of your Google preferred sources.

‌



Madueke has always looked better on the right wing, cutting onto his favored left foot. But he started on the left against Leeds and will probably do the same against Nottingham Forest on Sunday.

Arteta insists that Madueke can adapt and also be effective on either side especially as he can get some momentum with a run of games. Arteta said: “It’s down to necessities as well, sometimes, more than probably tactical decisions so far with him. I think he can play in both positions. He offers something completely different.

“Obviously now we have the necessity of a player on the left side with different qualities than Ebs as well, that can complement all the other unit we have on that left hand side. It’s great because he is comfortable there, he is enjoying playing there, and he is doing well. It’s a good solution.

‌



View 3 Images Noni Madueke joined Arsenal from Chelsea last summer (Image: Getty Images)

“That's what we want, players to be available and robust enough to be available always but if they're not, somebody else. The good thing is that when someone has come in, whether that's Ebs or Noni they have performed.”

Arteta has had a miserable recent record at Forest’s City Ground - just one win from five visits - and the last two have been two goalless draws. They will be looking to improve on that and Arteta says they must take encouragement from back to back wins since the international break.

‌



“We have responded really well in the last two games, two very good performances and results,” said Arteta. “Now we just focus on the game against Forest which I know is going to be a really tough one.”

View 3 Images Viktor Gyokeres has yet to score for Arsenal this season (Image: Getty Images)

There was also a challenge for Viktor Gyokeres who has yet to score for Arsenal this season and looks off the pace as he has been behind Kai Havertz in the pecking order. But Arteta says it is down to Gyokeres to repeat his prolific form for Sweden as he even made Nations League history by scoring in six consecutive games in the competition.

‌



Arteta added: “These are moments in a player's career, or in a season, I would say. And we are trying to help him as much as possible.

“The other day, I think, he had some very good moments. He's three or four times in front of goal with no keeper and the ball should arrive to him and it doesn't.

“And maybe you are talking about something else. But these are the strikers. It's very small margins. Scoring or not scoring changes the narrative, for sure not the perception of how much he can help the team.”

Sports.title: Enzo Maresca admits he may have to DROP Erling Haaland for Man City
Sports.content:
Enzo Maresca admits he may have to DROP Erling Haaland for Man City

Erling Haaland has started the season on fire by scoring 10 goals in nine games for Manchester City, but Enzo Maresca has admitted that his place in the starting XI isn't certain

View 2 Images Erling Haaland has started every game for club and country this season (Image: James Gill - Danehouse/Getty Images)

Manchester City boss Enzo Maresca has admitted that he may be forced to drop Erling Haaland and give him some rest. Haaland, 26, has enjoyed a typically prolific start to the season, despite an unusually busy summer.

‌



‌



The striker fired Norway to the quarter-finals of the World Cup in what was his first major tournament appearance with his country. Haaland started all four of Norway's games during the recent international break, and national team manager Stale Solbakken confirmed that his No.9 was fatigued after substituting him during their fourth and final match.

‌



Maresca acknowledges that Haaland needs time off to avoid injury, with City due to play Ipswich on Saturday and AEK Athens in the Champions League, also at home, next Tuesday. "At some point we probably need to give him rest, some days off," Maresca said in his pre-match press conference.

‌



"We are thinking about this not just with Erling because we have players, unfortunately or fortunately, they are playing all the games with us and all the games with the international teams. Elliot [Anderson], Enzo [Fernandez], Marc [Guehi], Erling, Ruben [Dias]. So at some point we probably need to give them some rest."

Haaland's double against Paris Saint-Germain in midweek put him on 10 goals in nine games for City this season. The Norwegian leads the Premier League scoring charts with six, one more than Chelsea's Joao Pedro.

City are top of the table with a 100 per cent record after six games. Victory over Ipswich would open up a six-point gap over defending champions Arsenal, who play on Sunday away to Nottingham Forest.

Maresca will have Phil Foden at his disposal following his red card against Manchester United prior to the international break. "Since his red card and the international break, it has been quite long, but he is training well and is very positive," the City boss added.

Can Enzo Maresca afford to rest Erling Haaland? Have your say in the comments section.

"We have so many games [coming up] so we will decide if he starts [on Saturday] or not. There is no doubt that he is going to give us something."

Ayyoub Bouaddi will be in contention to start against Ipswich after he impressed as a substitute on Wednesday. "I decided to go less physicality and more technical with Rayan [Cherki], but against these teams you need to be quite strong in the middle," Maresca explained.

"Bouaddi, Enzo and Elliot can for sure be a solution in the future. He is a fantastic player. When he is on the pitch, all the players around him improve. They are better players."

Sports.title: Peter Schmeichel reveals what really happened in Lisandro Martinez interview - 'Clumsy'
Sports.content:
Peter Schmeichel reveals what really happened in Lisandro Martinez interview - 'Clumsy'

Peter Schmeichel spoke to Lisandro Martinez moments after the Manchester United star made explosive comments in a separate interview following Tuesday's 2-0 defeat away to Atletico Madrid

View 2 Images Peter Schmeichel was caught off guard by Lisandro Martinez (Image: CBS Sports)

Peter Schmeichel has addressed criticism of his interview with Lisandro Martinez, admitting that it was 'clumsy'. Schmeichel spoke to Martinez moments after the Manchester United defender had, in a separate interview, slammed the club's leadership and called out director of football Jason Wilcox.

‌



‌



The 28-year-old was unhappy with their efforts in the summer transfer window in which United only signed four players. Martinez's comments came in an interview with Prime Video Sport's Gabriel Clarke after the Red Devils had lost 2-0 to Atletico Madrid in the Champions League.

‌



After speaking to Clarke, Martinez chatted with Schmeichel, who was working as CBS Sports' pitchside reporter at the Metropolitano. Fans on social media criticised the United legend for 'trying to be positive' as he attempted to shift the conversation to on-the-pitch matters.

‌



It turns out that Schmeichel didn't know the context behind Martinez's words. Appearing on The Overlap, sponsored by Sky Bet, he explained: "It's a bit of a weird one. My job is I do a couple of things to camera from the touchline, I'm there, I'm talking about the atmosphere and anything I've heard. And afterwards I go to the flash zone and do interviews.

Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

‌



"You're building relationships with the media people from the different clubs and you can say, 'I want to speak to him or him'. But at the end of the day they're not solely in charge of who you get to speak to UEFA also has media people on.

"There's one responsible for every team, then there's one above them, and everything has to go through them. When this happened, I'm actually next to TNT (sic), and Gabriel [Clarke] interviewed Lisandro Martinez. That interview is where everything came out.

"I know he's there, he's not on my list. I'm not interviewing him at all because I've asked for somebody else. This interview finishes and they push him into mine. So, when you look at the interview, I'm a little bit surprised. I don't know what he'd said at this time.

‌



"Then in interview with me he says, 'We should do a lot better'. He's carrying on from that interview, but I don't know what he's saying. Because he's speaking to a former player, I think he's saying that we, as players, should do a lot better.

Should Lisandro Martinez start against Leeds? Let us know your XI in the comments section.

View 2 Images Lisandro Martinez gave a bombshell interview to Gabriel Clarke (Image: Florencia Tan Jun - UEFA/UEFA via Getty Images)

‌



"I had no clue he was on the attack the way he was. So in my interview, I didn't understand that he was saying all that, so in a way my interview became a little bit clumsy in the greater scheme of things."

Joe Hart then asked Schmeichel what he'd have done differently had he known the full context. The former goalkeeper replied: "Definitely, I would've asked him if he felt that he was in a position to say that. I don't think players should ever come out and say anything like that."

United manager Michael Carrick confirmed on Friday that Martinez, who's been fined by the club and has issued an apology, will be part of the squad for Sunday's game against Leeds. Carrick insists that United have moved on from the drama and are focussed on getting their first win since September 10.

Sports.title: Red Roses' 41-game unbeaten run ended in dramatic fashion
Sports.content:
England's 41-game unbeaten run is over after they were stunned by a late rally from Canada, the Red Roses falling 24-21 in their WXV Global Series clash in Toronto.

Shoshanah Seumanutafa came off the bench to score the match-winning try in the 77th minute to hand England their first defeat since the 2022 World Cup final.

Following a draw in their previous clash last month in Exeter, Canada looked up for the challenge early as they opened the scoring through Savannah Bauder in the 15th minute.

Quickfire tries to Maddie Feaunati and Zoe Harrison just before half-time put England ahead 14-5 at the break.

The points kept flowing as both teams crossed just after play resumed, but DaLeaka Menin's 63rd-minute try kept the door open for Canada.

A raucous home crowd exploded for Seumanutafa's match-winner shortly after, with Canada able to hold on from there and quell England's historic run.

"I guess (the loss) frees us up and allows us all to find more.

"It was good to beat England, but I think for a few years now we knew ⁠that we could beat them. It was just a matter of time ​and a matter of putting every detail together."

"The bit we always remember is we're at the ​top, and when you're at the top, people want to bring you down as quick as ⁠they can," England captain Megan Jones said, adding that the team take "huge pride" in their unbeaten run.

Will Trenholm’s brace was not enough to help Gloucester pull off a stunning upset against Champions Cup holders Bordeaux, as they were forced to settle for a 36-36 draw after a dramatic contest.

George Skivington's team pushed the French outfit all the way during a pulsating European tie at Kingsholm Stadium.

Gloucester held a 24-17 lead at half-time before Trenholm crashed over twice, but a double by Louis Bielle-Biarrey salvaged a share of the spoils for visiting Bordeaux.

Sports.title: United States GP: UK schedule as F1 returns to COTA
Sports.content:
Following an extended stint across Asia, Formula 1 heads to America for the United States Grand Prix at the iconic Circuit of The Americas in Austin, Texas.

After the previous triple-header saw Kimi Antonelli move closer to a maiden F1 title, the Mercedes driver enters three more back-to-back races knowing he has every chance of sealing a historic triumph.

The Italian is 102 points clear of his Mercedes team-mate George Russell at the top of the standings, with the first two victories of the year for Red Bull and Max Verstappen only having helped Antonelli move clear of the pack, leaving him with a small chance of being crowned champion in Austin.

While both Antonelli and Mercedes are in remarkably strong positions in the championships, the competitive picture has rarely been more exciting during the 2026 season, with each of the top four teams entering each weekend with genuine hopes of victory.

Many eyes will be on Antonelli, but Verstappen's quest to complete a hat-trick of wins, along with Lewis Hamilton's attempts to bounce back from a tough Sunday in Singapore promise to provide plenty of entertainment.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player On the F1 Show podcast, Bernie Collins considers whether Lewis Hamilton has lost trust in Ferrari after overriding a team strategy call in Singapore.

United States GP track - Circuit of the Americas

Of the newer permanent circuits to have joined the calendar over the past couple of decades, the Circuit of the Americas is certainly one of the very best.

The undulating 3.4-mile, 20-corner layout built on the outskirts of Austin quickly proved a hit with drivers when it made its debut in 2021 as F1's first made-to-measure home in the USA.

There was also a sense of familiarity given its track design took inspiration from some of Europe's most famous tracks.

An Esses section reminiscent of Silverstone's legendary high-speed Maggotts and Becketts complex at Silverstone makes up Turns Three to Six, while a reverse triple-apex challenge in the style of Istanbul Park's Turn Eight and a Hockenheim-style arena section all feature in the exciting anti-clockwise lap.

The circuit even has its own signature feature in the form of a steep uphill run to the first corner, which has been the scene of numerous overtakes and controversial incidents over the past 13 years when drivers go wheel-to-wheel into the wide braking zone before powering back downhill towards the Esses.

United States GP weather in Austin

Temperatures are expected to climb above 30 degrees Celsius on all three days of track action, but the wild card is whether rain is going to play apart.

The latest forecast suggests there's a 50 per cent chance of rain falling during the race, with showers also possible on Friday and Saturday.

Sports.title: Usyk can return in world championship fight | 'Let's see who's best'
Sports.content:
Oleksandr Usyk could go straight into a world title fight on his return to boxing.

The unbeaten Ukrainian was the undisputed heavyweight champion but vacated all his belts and isn't expected to box again until next year.

But if he is planning a 'last dance' bout, promoter Frank Warren could provide a top-level opponent.

Warren promotes WBC champion Agit Kabayel, WBO heavyweight titlist Daniel Dubois and also represents Tyson Fury, who stands to win the WBA 'super' belt if can beat Anthony Joshua in December.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Take a look as Oleksandr Usyk and Tyson Fury took to social media, to tease a trilogy match-up between the two. IG credit: @usykaa, @tysonfury.

Usyk has beaten Fury and Dubois before, though a trilogy bout with either could still become a major fight.

Taking on Kabayel for the WBC crown at a stadium in Germany could also be appealing.

"I'll take that fight [for Kabayel], I wouldn't mind that fight," Warren told Sky Sports.

"Any of them," the promoter continued. "There are some great fights to be made and we'll make them.

"He can do what he likes," Warren said of Usyk, "but if he wants to fight one of these guys, then come and see us. It's not hard for us to do. We've worked together on quite a few occasions now, we got on very well and we've delivered.

"He'll want to be at the top so he'll want to fight the best ones so let's see who it is."

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Tyson Fury says he's using the Anthony Joshua fight as a warm-up to take on Oleksandr Usyk. Credit: FurociTV.

Dubois came unstuck on the previous occasions he fought Usyk. But he came roaring back to defeat Fabio Wardley in a thriller to win the WBO heavyweight title. If he can score a repeat victory over Wardley in their rematch at The O2 Arena in London, Dubois will look to take over next year as the best heavyweight in the world.

"That's the aim, that's our objective," Dubois' trainer Don Charles told Sky Sports. "It would be foolish of me to overlook Saturday.

"Fabio's a serious, serious fighter. A very determined fighter. He's ambitious, quite rightly so and he's a former world champion.

"He's going to do everything in his physical make up and desire to try and recapture his title and it's down to us say no you can't have it, we're having it for keeps."

Sports.title: McIlroy plays just four holes of second round due to bad light in India
Sports.content:
Rory McIlroy is four shots off the clubhouse lead but only four holes into his second round at the DP World India Championship after play was suspended early on Friday due to bad light in New Delhi.

Torrential rain on the Thursday resulted in a five-hour delay to the opening round, and there were further frustrations for those still out on the course when play was halted just before 6pm local time on Friday.

The second round is scheduled to restart at 6.45am on Saturday.

McIlroy, who is bidding to win the Race to Dubai title for a record-equalling eighth time, opened the tournament with a two-under 70 on Thursday, while he started his second round with an eagle to sit four under when play was stopped shortly after.

Dutchman Joost Luiten, who had to play 34 holes on Friday because of the delays, Angel Hidalgo and Alfred Dunhill Links Championship winner Adrian Meronk were all able to finish their second rounds, and top the leaderboard on eight under.

Belgian Thomas Detry is also eight under, but is only through six holes of his second round, for which he is currently three under.

England's Eddie Pepperell, who hit a six-under 66, and Todd Clements are both one shot back having also got into the clubhouse before the light faded.

Eugenio Chacarra is another at seven under, through five holes, as he looks for a strong finish to push his own challenge in the Race to Dubai rankings, currently sitting second.

Scotland's Robert MacIntyre was level par through five holes, also at four under overall, alongside defending champion Tommy Fleetwood, who was two under after four.

McIlroy was third in the DP World Tour standings coming into this penultimate event before the play-offs.

Leader Patrick Reed got through his second round at three under, recovering from a double-bogey at the fourth, but is level par overall.

Sports.title: Dubois and Wardley both career heaviest for heavyweight title rematch
Sports.content:
Both Daniel Dubois and Fabio Wardley weighed in at a career heaviest for their WBO heavyweight championship rematch.

London's Dubois had scaled a career heaviest for their first fight and he topped that at 253.9lbs for Saturday's rematch while Wardley was 248.3lbs.

Dubois said that means they're both going for power in this fight. "I'm ready to go, ready for my job," he told Sky Sports. "I'll break him down, break him down. Like last time, but better this time."

The Londoner halted Wardley in a frenetic first fight in May but the former champion excised the rematch clause in his contract in a bid to win back his title.

Wardley is fully expecting the same type of battle. "Knowing it's going to be a hard, hard fight is what gees me up, what keeps me going," he told Sky Sports.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Daniel Dubois is ready to get in the ring with Fabio Wardley and retain his WBO heavyweight title.

"It was well and truly something I came to terms with the second I pressed the button on the rematch clause. We're probably going back into the same kind of depths."

At Friday's weigh-in at Spitalfields Market in the heart of the City of London the two heavyweight rivals finished with a final face off, their last head-to-head encounter before Saturday's fight.

"I need to get through this to get to bigger things," Dubois declared. "I'm just ready to do my job on Saturday.

"Just want to go to work now."

Although Dubois won their first contest, his team insists he retains his singular focus.

His trainer Don Charles told Sky Sports: "Once he's in that mode, fight mode, he's in the zone and I love that from him.

"Once Daniel gets a fight date, he's locked in from that moment. He's a very intense athlete, intense character, he's a serious athlete. Everybody's got their different attributes. That's one of his strongest attributes.

"He doesn't have any outside distractions. That's refreshing."

Charles added: "We've prepared for a better version of Fabio. We have to anticipate for that. Because if you don't, that would be complacent of us and we don't have any complacency."

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Fabio Wardley is ready to seek revenge against Daniel Dubois and says he ‘isn’t picky’ about who he faces next if he can topple Dubois.

Both heavyweights appear confident. Promoter Frank Warren told Sky Sports: "That's the thing about these two guys, so much self-belief the pair of them, they both think they've got each other's number.

"And the one thing they can do, they can both punch and that's why this fight is going to be so exciting. It's definitely not going to go the distance."

Image: Dubois and Wardley have weighed in (Photos: Queensberry/Leigh Dawney)

'I just want all the belts'

Both men are looking forward to the biggest fights in the division. "It could lead on to unification fights. The landscape of heavyweight boxing is very different from when we had the first fight," Wardley told Sky Sports.

"The belts have been fragmented, the division's opened up, there's multiple world champions which then leads to multiple unification fights.

"Fury-AJ, of course, the winner there, there's a world title belt on the line there. There's [WBC titlist Agit] Kabayel, there's [IBF champion Filip] Hrgovic, I'm not particularly picky.

"I have no personal vendetta against any of these guys. I just want to hold all of them belts."

Sports.title: The All Blacks' Haka explained - plus rugby's other rituals
Sports.content:
One of the most intriguing and anticipated moments in the sport of rugby union: the sight of New Zealand's All Blacks performing their world-famous haka as the opposition stands before them.

But how much do you know about the haka? And also of the three other ceremonial war dances which take place in rugby: the Cibi, Siva Tau and Sipi Tau.

Find out everything you need to know below...

History of the haka in sport - When did it start? What does it mean?

An ancient traditional Māori practice, there is no single recorded date for the haka's first-ever performance owing to this very reason. It has been practised by indigenous Māori communities for centuries.

The earliest point at which Europeans witnessed the haka was the 18th century: Joseph Banks and James Cook on their first voyage to New Zealand in 1769 recorded the haka as "vigorous and ferocious".

In terms of its introduction into sport, New Zealand's first rugby union side visited Australia in Sydney in 1884 and performed the haka. During 1888/89, a 'New Zealand native team' toured the UK for the first time, performing the haka on October 3 1888 against Surrey in a tour match.

The year 1905 saw the birth of the 'All Blacks' as they toured Britain with a team which came to be known as 'The Originals.'

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player The All Blacks perform a spine-chilling haka at Ellis Park ahead of the opening Test against South Africa in the four-match Rugby's Greatest Rivalry series

The All Blacks performed their famous "Ka Mate" haka before Tests against Scotland and Wales, with it having been composed in 1820 by Māori chief Te Rauparaha.

Yet, the tradition of the All Blacks performing the haka on home soil and before every Test they played did not become custom until 1986.

Ahead of rugby's first World Cup in 1987, All Black Buck Shelford set about reforming the haka in order for pre-match performances to be organised, in sync and executed properly.

"If we're going to do it, we're going to do it right. Either perform the haka properly or not at all. Vote on it and decide which way you want to go," Shelford is said to have told team-mates at the time.

Shelford and team-mate Hika Reid subsequently taught and trained the All Blacks squad correct pronunciation of words and actions, and of the haka's importance.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player New Zealand captain Codie Taylor leads a spine-tingling haka for the first time against South Africa

At the 1987 World Cup in New Zealand, with Shelford now captain, the All Blacks performed the haka in New Zealand for the very first time, en route to the All Blacks clinching the trophy.

In terms of what the haka means, "Ka Mate" is the recitation of a traditional Māori poem about life, death and resilience.

The more common haka performed by the All Blacks today is the 'Kapa o Pango', first performed in August 2005 before a Tri-Nations Test against South Africa in Dunedin.

The haka featured an extended and aggressive introduction by team captain Tana Umaga, highlighted by a drawing of the thumb down the throat.

Famous haka responses - how should teams respond?

There have been a number of famous haka responses from opposition sides over the years.

In 1996, Australia famously (or infamously?) decided to totally ignore the haka altogether in Wellington, turning their backs on the All Blacks, following on from Wallabies great David Campese choosing to ignore the haka and do kicking drills ahead of the 1991 Rugby World Cup semi-final between the sides, which Australia won.

In 2019, England adopted a V-shaped formation in Yokohama ahead of their World Cup semi-final against the All Blacks. Once the haka started, English players progressed beyond the halfway line and held their ground as officials tried to move them.

Image: Facing the haka ahead of their 2019 Rugby World Cup semi-final in Japan, England stepped forward in a V-shaped formation

Image: England captain Owen Farrell smirked as the All Blacks performed the haka in Yokohama

England were later fined £2000 by World Rugby for breaching World Cup 2019 rules relating to cultural challenges, which stated no players from the team receiving the challenge may advance beyond the halfway line. England won the match 19-7 after a sensational performance.

World Rugby rules on haka responses World Rugby rules limit how close opposing teams can get to each other when facing the haka, a Maori war dance, and prevent them from crossing the halfway line. If both teams plan to perform a cultural challenge, a coin toss determines field positions. The winner can move up to the halfway line, while the other team must stay behind their own 10-metre line. If only one team is performing a challenge, the other team can't cross the halfway line, and the performing team can't cross their own 10-metre line. Teams that breach these rules can be fined. For example, in 2019 England were fined £2,000 for crossing the halfway line while facing New Zealand's haka in the Rugby World Cup semi-final. In 2011, France were fined £2,500 for advancing on New Zealand while they performed the haka before the World Cup final.

At the 2007 World Cup, France faced the All Blacks in a World Cup quarter-final in Cardiff, and memorably walked up in a line of opposition to the All Blacks, coming within a metre of the haka. France won the match 20-18.

France also marched forward in an arrow-formation facing the haka ahead of the 2011 Rugby World Cup final in New Zealand, before controversially losing 8-7 at Eden Park.

Image: France and New Zealand came within a metre of one another in a haka response before their 2007 World Cup quarter-final

Image: France also marched forward in an arrow-formation facing the haka ahead of the 2011 Rugby World Cup final

In 2005, the All Blacks agreed to a request from the Welsh Rugby Union to repeat the sequence of events from the original match a century before in 1905, which involved the haka taking place after the New Zealand national anthem but before the Welsh one.

A year later in 2006, Wales demanded a repeat of the sequence, which the All Blacks refused, ultimately performing the haka in the dressing rooms and not in front of the watching fans. Then All Blacks captain Richie McCaw defended the decision by stating the haka was "integral to New Zealand culture and the All Blacks' heritage" and "if the other team wants to mess around, we'll just do the haka in the shed."

Two years later in 2008, another memorable Wales vs New Zealand haka situation unfolded, as following the conclusion of the haka in Cardiff, Wales refused to break and move until the All Blacks did. Neither side did for nearly a minute-and-a-half despite urging from referee Jonathan Kaplan, until McCaw instructed the All Blacks to break off. Wales led 9-6 at half-time but were eventually well beaten 29-9.

Image: Wales and New Zealand held their ground for over 80 seconds following the conclusion of the haka in 2008

Image: Referee Jonathan Kaplan attempted to make both sides move in Cardiff in 2008, but failed

In 2016, Ireland faced the All Blacks in Chicago seeking a first-ever win over New Zealand in 111 years. Just weeks prior, Munster coach Anthony Foley had died in his sleep in Paris at the age of 42 ahead of a European Cup contest against Racing 92.

Facing the haka, Ireland lined up in a figure of eight in memory of Foley, a former Ireland and Munster No 8 in his playing days. Ireland went on to clinch a stunning 40-29 maiden win over the All Blacks.

Before their 2023 Rugby World Cup quarter-final, Ireland repeated the same haka response, but lost to the All Blacks in Paris 28-24.

Image: Ireland lined up in a figure of eight to face the haka in memory of the late Anthony Foley ahead of victory in 2016 and defeat in 2023

In 2008, a uniquely stirring haka response took place at Thomond Park in Limerick as Munster quartet Doug Howlett, Rua Tipoki, Lifeimi Mafi and Jeremy Manning stepped forward to perform a haka facing the All Blacks with the rest of their Munster team-mates stood behind them.

Image: Munster's Rua Tipoki (left), Doug Howlett (centre) and Lifeimi Mafi (right) stepped forward to perform a memorable haka against the All Blacks at Thomond Park in 2008

A similar event took place recently in 2026 when All Blacks great Ma'a Nonu performed a solo haka facing the All Blacks while a player for South African club side the Sharks, ahead of New Zealand's tour match in Durban.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Ma'a Nonu gave his former All Blacks team-mates the ultimate show of respect by responding to their haka with one of his own

Are New Zealand only nation that perform the haka?

While the haka is rugby's best-known and most famous traditional pre-match ceremonial war dance, the island nations of Fiji, Samoa and Tonga all also perform their own versions.

Fiji perform the Cibi, which sees the team stand in formation and led by a vocal soloist, before dropping into a synchronised low crouch or knee-bend while making aggressive arm and hand gestures, concluding with an explosive jump or step-up.

Image: Fiji perform the Cibi during an Autumn Nations Series 2025 Test against Scotland at Murrayfield

Image: Australia watch on as Fiji perform the Cibi at the 2023 Rugby World Cup

Samoa perform the Siva Tau, with the ritual led by a designated chanter and players starting in a lowered or kneeling stance before rising into synchronised movements that include chest-slapping, foot-stomping, aggressive gestures, and intense vocal chanting.

Image: Samoa's players perform the Siva Tau at the 2023 Rugby World Cup in France

Tonga perform the Sipi Tau, which begins with the team huddled or kneeling in a circle led by a central caller, before breaking into a structured formation on the field featuring deep squats, chest-pounding, rhythmic foot-stomping, and aggressive synchronised gestures.
