“Under present case law, it seems unlikely that a company such as OpenAI would be held to have such duties to warn,” Choi told Al Jazeera. “The chatbot is not a licensed therapist. There is no special relationship between the company and the victims.”

Choi said existing negligence and product liability laws could potentially be applied to AI companies, but proving responsibility would present significant challenges.

Finding a balance

Fordham’s Sharma suggested that independent institutions could help establish reporting standards rather than leaving decisions entirely to private companies or requiring immediate disclosure to police.

Such bodies she said could develop procedures for assessing threats and explore ways of sharing only relevant information while protecting users’ identities and other personal details.

Meanwhile, Younes argued that users should, at a minimum, be clearly informed about whether their conversations are monitored and what circumstances could lead to information being shared with law enforcement.

“This is almost certainly an issue that will be wrestled with over the coming years, and I’m not sure anyone knows the solution at this particular point in time,” she said.

“Events that have not yet occurred will likely influence how these policies are shaped.”

World.title: Russian attacks in Ukraine kill at least 8, cut power to 1 million
World.content:
Russia strikes Kharkiv, Kramatorsk, Volyn and Rivne as Russia presses its campaign against Ukraine’s power grid.

Share Russian attacks in Ukraine kill at least 8, cut power to 1 million on social media

Russian attacks killed at least eight people and injured 60 across Ukraine, hit two shopping centres and cut power to more than a million people, Ukrainian officials have said.

The attacks on Friday struck nine regions. In the eastern city of Kharkiv, a 71-year-old woman and a 58-year-old man were killed and 12 people were wounded in strikes on three districts, Governor Oleh Syniehubov said.

Two people were killed in Kramatorsk, a frontline city in the Donetsk region, and two more in the southeastern Dnipropetrovsk region.

In the northwestern Volyn region, which borders Poland, a drone strike on a food-processing facility killed one person and wounded eight, Governor Roman Romaniuk said.

Drones also hit a customs terminal and set fire to about 10 trucks in the town of Kovel, on a major road from Kyiv to Poland.

In Rivne, drones hit a major shopping centre and other sites, killing one person and wounding seven, regional governor Oleksandr Koval said.

A shopping centre in Sumy, close to the front line, was also hit.

Power cuts

Ukraine’s Ministry of Energy said repair crews had restored power to more than a million people who lost it on Friday.

In Volyn, about 370,000 households lost power, with supply since restored to at least 100,000 of them.

The blackout could last at least 24 hours in the regional capital, Lutsk, Mayor Andriy Razumovskyi said.



Large parts of Rivne were also left without power.

Russia’s military chief told President Vladimir Putin on Friday that the military had allocated the assets needed to press its aerial campaign against Ukraine’s energy system.

Civilian toll

Meanwhile, the United Nations said on Friday that civilian casualties in Ukraine had climbed steeply.

According to UN human rights monitors, at least 328 civilians were killed and 2,105 wounded in Ukraine last month, 85 percent more than in September 2025.

Between January and September 2026, 2,570 civilians were killed and 15,211 wounded, almost 60 percent more than in the same period last year and more than twice the 2024 level, the report said.

“The first two weeks of October were among the deadliest periods for civilians in years,” said Danielle Bell, head of the UN’s human rights monitoring mission in Ukraine.

World.title: Three Mexicans jailed for 158 years each for killing Australian, US surfers
World.content:
A Mexican judge sentenced the three men for the 2024 murders a week after they were found guilty.

Share Three Mexicans jailed for 158 years each for killing Australian, US surfers on social media

Three Mexican men have been sentenced to more than 158 years in prison each for the murder of two Australian brothers and their American friend during a surf trip on Mexico’s Baja California coast in 2024.

A Mexican judge in the coastal city of Ensenada, in Baja California state, ruled on Friday that Jesus Gerardo Garcia, alias “El Kekas”, Irineo Francisco “N” and Angel Jesus “N” would each serve 158 years and nine months in prison for homicide, robbery with violence and vehicle theft with violence.

The defendants were found guilty a week ago of the murders of Australian brothers Callum and Jake Robinson, aged 33 and 30, respectively, and their American friend Jack Carter Rhoad, 30.

The case impacted Mexico’s tourism industry by exposing the risks foreigners face when visiting the country.

Previously, the Baja California State Attorney General’s Office requested the “exemplary sentence” of 210 years in prison for each defendant.

Antonio Otanez, president of the Baja California surfers’ association, welcomed the outcome, saying “justice has been served.”

Otanez acknowledged that the killings had caused a “major drop” in tourist visits, particularly by surfers, to the region known for its beautiful beaches.

The Robinson brothers and Rhoad travelled to Mexico in late April 2024 to surf at a beach in Punta San Jose, near the popular tourist city of Ensenada.

The three friends camped on the beach on the night of April 27, 2024. Authorities launched a multi-day search with help from the US Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI) after the men were missing for several days.



The bodies were found on May 3 in a well more than 15 metres (50 feet) deep, all with gunshot wounds to their heads.

Last week, the brothers’ father, Martin Robinson, said the “guilty verdict is a significant moment in our long and painful journey to seek justice for our beautiful sons, Callum and Jake, and their friend Carter Rhoad, whose lives were so cruelly taken from them in 2024.”

World.title: The Israeli politicians seeking to replace Netanyahu
World.content:
A look at Israel’s main opposition leaders, their parties and their largely shared positions on Gaza and other wars before October 27 election.

On September 26, five leading members of Israel’s self-styled Zionist opposition signed a non-aggression pact, seeking to oust incumbent Benjamin Netanyahu in the October 27 election.

Gathered at the Tel Aviv home of opposition leader Yair Lapid were his co-runner, former Prime Minister Naftali Bennett, leader of Beyachad; former Chief of Staff Gadi Eisenkot, leader of the new Yashar party; Yair Golan, leader of the Democrats party; and Avigdor Liberman, head of the Yisrael Beiteinu party.

In the statement of principles published after the hours-long meeting, the leaders said, “Despite ideological differences among us, the formation of a Zionist, statesmanlike government dedicated to repair and reconstruction is our shared overarching goal.”

However, whether they offer meaningful change in substance as well as style, or which one of them might lead a future coalition, remains open to question.

With the exception of Golan, all take a fundamentally right-wing approach to Israel’s challenges.

None is committed to establishing a Palestinian state, with only the Democrats acknowledging it as a distant, unspecified goal. None, Golan included, accepts that Israel’s war on Gaza amounts to genocide or that it has committed war crimes in killing more than 74,000 people there. Nor has any questioned Israeli military actions against Lebanon, Syria, Yemen, Qatar and Iran, instead reserving criticism mostly for how those actions have allowed Israel to be perceived internationally.



“The dominant forces in the opposition such as Bennett, Liberman or Eisenkot represent right-wing politics,” said Ahron Bregman, an Israeli analyst and senior teaching fellow at King’s College London. “They are not willing to touch the real, fundamental issue which is at the heart of everything: the Palestinian issue, and the Palestinian aspirations for independence.” He likened them to Netanyahu, but without the corruption allegations and support of far-right figures, such as National Security Minister Itamar Ben-Gvir and Finance Minister Bezalel Smotrich. “Israel as a whole is a right-wing nation,” he added.

So, who are the main opposition figures and what do their parties stand for?

Gadi Eisenkot – Yashar

Credited with originating the Dahiyeh Doctrine in 2008, involving “disproportionate force” and large-scale destruction of civilian infrastructure against groups such as Hezbollah and Hamas, Eisenkot served as Israeli military chief from 2015 to 2019.

The 66-year-old entered politics in 2022 with former Defence Minister Benny Gantz’s National Unity alliance and later joined the war cabinet assembled by Netanyahu after the Hamas-led attacks in southern Israel on October 7, 2023. In December that year, his son Gal, 25, and two nephews were killed while participating in the genocide in Gaza, losses commentators say have helped forge a connection with an electorate that has come to see itself as scarred by war.

In June 2024, he quit the war cabinet alongside Gantz, accusing Netanyahu of lacking a strategy to end the war. A year later, Eisenkot founded the centrist Yashar (Straight/Honest), advocating for professional government, military service for all – including ultra-Orthodox Jews – and a state commission of inquiry into the failings before October 7.

While notoriously ambiguous on many of Israel’s foreign policy positions, he has been critical of the government’s reliance upon the United States in achieving its war aims, while not questioning those aims themselves. In June, he characterised Washington’s mediated negotiations with Tehran to end the war against Iran that Washington had embarked upon with Israel as “a deal taking shape far from here and far from Israeli interests” and, the same month, railed against US restrictions on Israel’s freedom of action in Lebanon.

Eisenkot has ruled out including the United Arab List, or Ra’am party, in a post-election coalition. In a September 26 Channel 12 interview, he said no Arab party would accept his conditions, including recognition of Israel as a Jewish state.

Naftali Bennett, Yair Lapid – Beyachad

Beyachad (Together) is the joint list announced in April 2026 by former Prime Ministers Naftali Bennett and Yair Lapid, who served for a combined 18 months in 2021-2022 between Netanyahu governments.



Bennett, a 54-year-old longtime supporter of illegal settlements in the occupied West Bank, leads the list, with Lapid, the 62-year-old founder of the centrist Yesh Atid party, in second place.

Lapid has called his partner “a right-wing politician, but an honest one”. Neither has prioritised resolving the Israeli-Palestinian conflict or supported a Palestinian state. Though their 2021 coalition included Ra’am, Bennett has acknowledged that this broke an electoral promise.

Lapid has been one of Israel’s most outspoken critics of how its genocide and multiple strikes upon its neighbours are perceived internationally, while rarely questioning the rationale behind those actions. Bennett, in contrast, is more outspoken in his hawkish views. A full-throated supporter of the country’s war on Iran, he also congratulated Israel’s military and security services for a September 2025 attack on Qatar’s capital, Doha, that targeted senior Hamas leaders as they met to consider a Gaza ceasefire proposal put forth by the US. A Qatari security official was killed in the attack, which drew condemnation from across the region and beyond.

They now seek a government composed solely of Zionist parties, also ruling out reliance on Arab parties.

Avigdor Lieberman – Yisrael Beiteinu

The most hawkish voice at Lapid’s table, Lieberman, 68, founded Yisrael Beiteinu (Israel Our Home) in 1999 to represent right-leaning Russian-speaking immigrants.

Once Netanyahu’s protege, Lieberman has ruled out serving under him or joining a coalition that includes the ultra-Orthodox or relies on Arab parties, which he calls anti-Zionist. He has also rejected a minority government, reportedly making him a principal obstacle to Eisenkot becoming the bloc’s prime ministerial candidate.

In November 2023, Lieberman repeated his 2018 assertion, made then as defence minister, that there were “no innocents in Gaza”. In February, he visited the Karem Abu Salem crossing, known as Kerem Shalom to Israelis, and accused Netanyahu’s government of funding Hamas by allowing the minimal humanitarian aid that has been permitted into Gaza.

The Yisrael Beiteinu leader has been a consistent supporter of Israel’s genocide and subsequent military actions. In September 2025, he joined other Israeli politicians in criticising Netanyahu for the apology to Doha that he had been forced to make by the Trump administration for that month’s strike, saying the apology was instead owed to the Israeli public. Equally, he has argued against any restraint in its invasion of Lebanon, telling the Jerusalem Post in March: “If once again we go for a limited operation, some manoeuvre near the border, maybe talk about a security zone, it’s complete madness.”

“Lieberman does not belong in this bloc,” said Shaiel Ben-Ephraim, an Israeli analyst with Atlas Global Strategies, arguing that his main motivation was hatred of Netanyahu.

However, Ben-Ephraim said, Lieberman “maintains a loyal base and is a crucial force in Israeli politics”. His core constituency is the former Soviet electorate, but he has gained wider trust through his perceived independence.



Observers say he could potentially return to Netanyahu’s right-wing bloc.

Yair Golan – Democrats

The only leader at Lapid’s table from the Zionist left and the only one open to working with Palestinian parties, Golan heads the Democrats, a liberal party that was formed in 2024 through the merger of Labor and the social democratic, secular Meretz.

A retired major-general and former deputy chief of staff, Golan, 64, earned domestic plaudits for driving south during the 2023 Hamas-led attack and helping repel it.

Golan is alone among many in the anti-Netanyahu bloc in his criticism of the government’s war aims, arguing that military achievements are being squandered without a coherent diplomatic and political strategy

In May 2025, two years into the genocide in Gaza, Golan sparked controversy when he told a news conference that a “sane country does not kill babies as a hobby”, accusing ministers of celebrating the starvation of Palestinian children in the territory. He later walked back the comments after widespread criticism in Israel. In October, while praising the achievements of the previous year’s 12-day war against Iran, he told party members that the assassination of Iranian Supreme Leader Ali Khamenei at the beginning of the conflict was a “mistake”. “Not because he didn’t deserve to die,” he caveated, “only because it doesn’t serve the interests of the State of Israel.”

Despite his openness to working with Palestinian parties, in September, Golan backed the disqualification of Sami Abu Shehadeh, leader of the Arab Balad party, over an article about October 7, drawing criticism from the Joint List – an alliance of the Arab-led Hadash, Ta’al and Balad parties – and commentators.

Roi Zur, a University of Essex specialist in Israeli politics, said that despite Golan and Lieberman’s ideological differences on security and conflict, there will be “no winning coalition without these two”. He added that concerns about a clash between them miss the point, noting that both oppose Netanyahu, favour secularisation and strongly oppose exemptions from military service for ultra-Orthodox Jews.

World.title: Brazil sees record fall in Amazon deforestation as key election looms
World.content:
Brazil's government says deforestation rates in the country's Amazon and savanna regions have fallen to record lows ahead of a presidential election run-off in which the rainforest's future is a key issue.

Left-wing President Luiz InÃ¡cio Lula da Silva, when he assumed office three years ago, pledged to end deforestation by 2030 in the Amazon. It had surged under his right-wing predecessor, Jair Bolsonaro.

Lula will face Bolsonaro's son Flavio in the run-off on 25 October, with polls suggesting a neck-and-neck race. Flavio is expected to continue his father's policies if he wins, though he has pledged to fight organised crime in the Amazon.

Satellite data shows that in the year to July 2026, the deforestation rate fell by 41.8% in the Amazon - the biggest drop since records began in 1988. The fall in the Cerrado, Brazil's savanna region, was 23.8%.

The Amazon rainforest - the world's largest - is a crucial buffer in the global fight against climate change and 60% of it is located in Brazil.

World.title: Trump waives several Russia sanctions as row with Zelensky intensifies
World.content:
Donald Trump has blocked numerous sanctions on Russia two days before they were due to take effect, as a row with his Ukrainian counterpart Volodymyr Zelensky deepens.

The sanctions were passed by the US Congress and signed into law by Trump in September.

But the US president issued an executive order on Friday night saying that suspending some was in the US "national interest", prompting a backlash from US lawmakers.

Relations between Washington and Kyiv frayed this week, after the US struck a controversial deal to import Russian diesel. Ukraine then accused the Trump administration of withdrawing key military support.

Trump and Zelensky have exchanged sharp words about one another throughout the week. Ukraine's president barbed that it was nice to be among "real leaders" while addressing an EU summit, after Trump said he was "more difficult to deal with" than Russian President Vladimir Putin.

The new US sanctions law took aim at Russia's economy, giving Trump broad powers to levy tariffs of up to 100% on imports from the top five purchasers of Russian oil and gas â most significantly China and India.

It also included sanctions against senior Russian figures, including Putin, as well as Russian financial institutions and Moscow's so-called "shadow fleet" of vessels used to circumvent existing embargoes.

Many of these provisions have now been waived by Trump.

Democrats such as the Virginia Congressman Don Beyer have already criticised Trump's sanctions move, accusing him of capitulating to Moscow and turning his back on Kyiv and Zelensky.

"Trump's latest surrender to Putin again betrays our Ukrainian partners and defies clear congressional intent of legislation designed to punish Russia for its illegal war of aggression," Beyer wrote on X.

The move is also likely to draw criticism from Ukraine, where Zelensky has long stressed the need for tighter international sanctions to limit funding Russia can use in its war effort.

Trump initially drew criticism from Zelensky and Ukraine's European allies for temporarily suspending some US sanctions to import Russian diesel as a latest effort to bring down US energy prices, which have skyrocketed during the Iran war.

Trump has spent months grappling with the political consequences of the Middle East conflict - which has sent fuel costs, in particular diesel, soaring - ahead of the US midterm elections. Rising inflation has soured Trump's standing with the American public.

Zelensky suggested the deal was tantamount to the US investing in Russia's war effort.

World.title: Oregon teacher fought school attacker before armed dad shot suspect 'multiple times'
World.content:
Some readers may find this article distressing.

An Oregon teacher threw her mobile phone before she tackled and attempted to disarm a teenager who opened fire on a special educational needs class.

As she tried to wrestle a shotgun off him on the floor of the classroom - where three children and a teacher were killed - a bystander armed with a pistol ran inside and killed the teen.

The bystander, a father of two girls at the school, had been driving past Silver Rail Elementary in Bend at lunchtime on Thursday when he saw the suspect firing in the school's car park and then shooting through a window to enter.

Police said the 16-year-old suspected attacker used to be a student at the school.

Police say he had been armed with about 44 more rounds of shotgun ammunition when he was stopped. He fired as many as 15 rounds in the class.

"To the people who showed courage in the face of such violence and intervened to prevent this tragedy from being any worse, we owe you a debt of gratitude," Bend Police Chief Mike Krantz said.

Police offered more information on the attack at a news conference on Friday, where they identified two of the four victims. They include five-year-old Rhoam Summer and 25-year-old teacher Meghan Lambert.

Lambert's family said in a statement shared by the police that her goal was to be a teacher in the district in which she grew up and that she was "compassionate and had a huge heart".

"She always fought for the underdog and those with special needs," they said.

Bryan Jolly, Summer's grandfather, said the family was devastated by his death.

"The whole thing is senseless, and a shock," he told the New York Times, saying his grandson was "was very bright and very mischievous and very fun-loving, and totally without fear".

The families of the two other students who were killed, an eight-year-old and 11-year-old, did not wish to have them publicly identified yet, police said.

Two others were injured in the attack. Another teacher, a 54-year-old, was still being treated at hospital, and a seven-year-old student, who was in serious but stable condition.

World.title: Three men jailed for 158 years each for murdering Australian and US surfers in Mexico
World.content:
A Mexican judge has sentenced three men convicted of murdering Australian brothers Jake and Callum Robinson and their US friend Carter Rhoad to 158 years and nine months in jail each.

The Robinsons and Rhoad were killed in an apparent botched robbery of their truck on a secluded beach in Baja California in 2024 while they were on a surfing trip, the court heard during the trial.

The murders sent shockwaves around the world, particularly in Australia, as the area is usually safe from the violence seen in other parts of Mexico.

The guilty verdict was handed down last week. Debra Robinson, the brothers' mother, told the courtroom that her sons' murders had taken "the future we had imagined with them".

The convicted killers' full names were not given for legal reasons, meaning they were only identified as JesÃºs Gerardo, Irineo Francisco and Ãngel JesÃºs.

In November last year, the girlfriend of the alleged ringleader, JesÃºs Gerardo (alias "El Kekas"), was sentenced in a separate trial to 20 years in prison. She had admitted to involvement in the robbery.

The court heard that the bodies of the victims were found dumped down a well with gunshot wounds to their heads.

At the time, the murders shocked locals and tourists in the beach town of Ensenada who were disturbed at the apparent ease and sheer pointlessness of the killings.

Ensenada has a reputation as a welcoming spot for surfers, but the chilling murders revealed how commonplace such extreme violence remains in Mexico.

The only explanation the authorities were able to give was that the surfers - all in their early 30s - had ultimately been murdered for being in the wrong place at the wrong time.

Their killings happened barely 36 hours after they crossed into Mexico from the US. Their bodies, however, were not found for another week, when their families were able to identify them.

Local surfers also called for greater security for residents and visiting tourists, citing other recent examples of violence in the state. Tourism is a key part of the regional economy in Baja California.

World.title: Inside Ukrainian offensive pushing Russia back - with Starlink playing a key role
World.content:
A Russian drone zips across the computer screen, startling the commanders keeping watch over the battlefield via a live stream in their bunker.

Cigarette in one hand, radio in the other, one of them calls in their own drone to bring it down and warns the soldiers below of the threat. The men are dangerously exposed, on the long walk across open ground from their front line positions. They are being replaced after three months forcing the Russians back.

This is part of Operation Vivaldi, a Ukrainian counter-offensive which they say has liberated 277 sq km (106 square miles) in the eastern Donbas region in recent months.

The name reflects the offensive's four stages, or seasons - like the Italian composer's violin concerto. The successful assault blunted an attempted Russian pincer movement that threatened to encircle the key Fortress Belt cities still under Ukrainian control.

While Russia this month pummels Ukraine from the air, crippling its energy infrastructure and killing scores of civilians across the country, at the front, it is Ukraine that has made recent gains. Kyiv says it has inflicted heavy losses - 8,000 Russian casualties in Vivaldi alone, and close to 50,000 along the front in the month of September â and suffered few casualties in return.

World.title: Palestinians and US journalist injured by Israeli settlers in West Bank harvest attack
World.content:
Dozens of masked settlers have attacked Palestinians and set fire to cars and olive trees during the annual olive harvest in the occupied West Bank.

A BBC team witnessed one of several attacks in farmland near the Palestinian village of Abu Falah. A local official said the attacks had injured 12 Palestinians, including four dual Palestinian American citizens. A foreign journalist was also among those hurt.

Driving into the area early in the morning, we came across the first signs of the violence: a stream of cars carrying wounded Palestinian olive farmers racing out along the narrow stony track, piled high with olive picking equipment, as smoke rose from several fires nearby.

The bloodied face of Majdi Fheed peered out from the backseat of one car.

"We were getting our olive trees and almost 15 Jewish guys â¦ started attacking us with guns, with rocks, with special weapons. They hit me on my head [and] my neck â look, I am bleeding!"

Yaser AlKam, a council member from the neighbouring village of Turmus Aya told me Majdi - an American citizen - was attacked by settlers with nail-studded sticks, and needed treatment for deep wounds on his head. His elderly mother was also injured.

Another man ferrying the injured to hospital told us that settlers had attacked them with sticks while they harvested their olives, and had burned three cars â including one of his own.

"As soon as we got to the land and put our things on the ground, they started to come, so we ran away" said a woman next to him.

World.title: Katie Zacharia leaving White House role less than five days into job
World.content:
Katie Zacharia will be leaving her post as White House press secretary, just five days after her shaky public debut.

US President Donald Trump told reporters moments before news of her exit was announced that he had told her "you don't have to do this if you don't want to" and "honestly, if I were you, I'd reconsider".

Zacharia faced heavy criticism for her first press briefing on Tuesday, which lasted less than 15 minutes and included only three questions from reporters.

She spent the days following playing defence, fielding tough questions from news outlets about her credentials and preparedness for the job.

Trump hinted at her impending exit early on Friday afternoon, during an impromptu news conference in front of the Marine One helicopter.

"I said, 'Is this for you, Katie? Because honestly, you don't need this'," Trump said.

"You don't have to be treated this badly," he continued, adding that he believed she had been treated "pretty nastily" by the media.

Hours later, praised Trump as "kind, wonderful, gracious, thoughtful, enthusiastic, and the most hardworking man" on X, writing that it had been an honour to work for him.

As the November midterm elections, which will decide who controls the US Congress, draw closer, Democrats are seizing on Zacharia's abrupt departure as a sign of failure in the Republican White House.

"The White House Press Secretary is gone. Maga extremists continue to fall apart," the top Democrat in the House of Representatives, Hakeem Jeffries, posted on X.

Zacharia appeared visibly nervous during her inaugural White House press briefing, in which she read talking points from a notebook, answered only a few questions and referred to her husband as the president.

During the briefing, a reporter asked Zacharia - who had been called an attorney by Trump and others and who graduated from Pepperdine University's law school - about where she passed the bar exam. To practice law in the US, an attorney must be admitted to a state's bar association by passing a rigorous exam.

"When I was in China," she replied.

After intense scrutiny and digging by the media, Zacharia admitted on Thursday that she did not pass the bar exam.

She did say in a statement that she had practised international transaction law in China with the "appropriate credentials".

Questions about her legal credentials became a major talking point throughout the week, with Sean Hannity, from conservative-leaning Fox News, lobbing particularly pointed questions at her during an interview on Thursday.

When she said she had not passed the bar, he replied: "Why didn't you just say, 'I never practiced law?'"

Zacharia also described how quickly she had taken on the press secretary role - having been hired less than a week before her debut - prompting him to ask: "Am I hearing that you think the staff should have better prepped you?"

When she appeared on Fox & Friends, which Trump often watches, on Friday, Zacharia faced a similar line of questioning.

She told the show's hosts that she did not disclose to Trump that she was not an attorney, because "those questions weren't asked", saying she was hired for a communications role, not a legal one.

Host Lawrence Jones then asked her: "Do you think you still have the confidence of the president?"

She avoided offering a direct answer but ended by saying: "I hope to be able to build the confidence and trust of everyone around me."

Zacharia's early exit is the quickest among Trump's White House press team.

In the president's first term, Anthony Scaramucci left his post as White House communications director after only 10 days.

"Records are made to be broken," Scaramucci wrote on X on Friday. "But I take no pleasure in other people's pain."

World.title: Trump 'completely wrong' to restrict support for Ukraine, Italian minister tells BBC
World.content:
Italy's defence minister has said it was a "complete mistake, a major mistake" for the US to limit access to satellite systems and intelligence used by Ukraine to defend itself against Russian attacks.

Guido Crosetto warned in a BBC interview that any such move by US President Donald Trump's administration "makes absolutely no sense" and risked prolonging Russia's full-scale invasion rather than helping to bring peace.

US officials have said Trump has not asked for the slowdown of internet speeds the US provides to Ukraine and which are vital for its war effort. Trump has also denied that the US has stopped sharing early-warning alerts of incoming Russian aerial attacks with Ukraine.

Crosetto's comments continue Italy's sharpening criticism of the US.

Earlier this week, Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni called Trump's deal to buy diesel from Russia a "very risky choice" and said it would "grant Russia legitimacy" as it bombed cities in Ukraine.

Trump agreed the deal with Russian President Vladimir Putin, blaming Kyiv's own attacks on Russian refineries for rising fuel prices.

Meloni, once considered so close to the US president she was dubbed a "Trump whisperer", said the move ran counter to efforts to bring Putin to the negotiating table.

"Peace will come when Putin is convinced there is a stalemate, that he cannot advance any further," her defence minister told the BBC at his ministry building in Rome.

Crosetto was a co-founder of Meloni's hard-right Fratelli d'Italia party, which has led a right-wing government coalition since 2022, shortly after the start of Russia's full-scale war.

"If [Putin] sees weakness on the Ukrainian side â and if the US deprives Ukraine of resources, that creates weakness â then he will believe he can win. So he will continue the war," Crosetto warned.

"I think that is completely wrong."

World.title: FIFA U-17 Women’s World Cup, Day One Preview: Germany take on Argentina as Nigeria open against Poland
World.content:
The FIFA U-17 Women’s World Cup Morocco 2026 gets underway on Saturday with four intriguing fixtures at the Mohammed VI Football Complex in Rabat, as emerging talents from across the world begin their quest for global glory.

From Germany’s pursuit of a first title to the defending champions DPR Korea’s bid to extend their dominance, the opening day promises a compelling mix of ambition, history and fresh beginnings.

Hosts Morocco will also take centre stage as they welcome New Zealand. Meanwhile, Nigeria’s Flamingos begin their campaign against Poland in a Group B encounter that offers an early test of their championship credentials.

With four matches spread across the complex’s four pitches, the tournament’s opening day will offer an early glimpse of the teams that can make a strong impression in Morocco.

Germany vs Argentina: European experience meets South American ambition

Group A | Mohammed VI Football Complex, Pitch 1, Rabat

Germany begin their campaign against debutants Argentina, with both sides eager to make a strong statement in their opening fixture.

The Germans are appearing at the FIFA U-17 Women’s World Cup for the eighth time, but a maiden title remains their ultimate target. After missing the previous edition, they secured their return by defeating France in the final of the UEFA Women’s U-17 Championship.

Their experience at this level could prove valuable, but Argentina arrive highly motivated.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

The South Americans have waited almost two decades to reach the tournament for the first time, finally securing their place after reaching the final of the South American U-17 Women’s Championship.

For Argentina, the occasion offers a chance to make their mark on the global stage. For Germany, it is the first step in another attempt to turn their pedigree into a world title.

The clash will test whether Argentina can translate their continental progress into success against one of Europe’s established youth football nations.

DPR Korea vs Puerto Rico: Defending Champions begin Title defence

Group B | Mohammed VI Football Complex, Pitch 2, Rabat

Puerto Rico could hardly have asked for a more demanding introduction to their first FIFA U-17 Women’s World Cup as they prepare to face two-time reigning champions DPR Korea.

The Caribbean nation have made history by qualifying for the tournament for the first time, finishing as the best second-placed team during CONCACAF U-17 Women’s World Cup qualifying.

Their achievement marks a significant milestone for Puerto Rican women’s football, but the challenge awaiting them in Rabat is formidable.

DPR Korea arrive as the team to beat after winning their fifth AFC U-17 Women’s Asian Cup title in May. The reigning champions will now seek another historic feat: becoming the first nation to win three consecutive FIFA 11-a-side World Cup titles.

Their recent continental triumph underlines the quality and consistency they bring into the competition, and they will be eager to establish their authority from the opening whistle.

Puerto Rico, meanwhile, will need composure, organisation and belief to withstand the pressure. Their debut alone represents a major achievement, but a positive result against the champions would deliver one of the tournament’s earliest shocks.

Morocco vs New Zealand: Hosts seek stronger start on Home soil

Group A | Mohammed VI Football Complex, Pitch 3, Rabat

Hosts Morocco will look to make home advantage count as they face New Zealand, with the North Africans determined to start their campaign on a stronger note than they did at the previous edition.

Morocco suffered consecutive defeats at the start of last year’s tournament. As they enter their second of five consecutive hosting appearances, a positive opening result would be important for building confidence and energising the home crowd.

New Zealand also have a point to prove on the global stage. The Young Football Ferns have gone nine matches without a victory at the FIFA U-17 Women’s World Cup, a run they will be desperate to end in Morocco.

However, their regional form offers encouragement. New Zealand stormed to the OFC U-16 Women’s Championship title with five consecutive victories, demonstrating the attacking quality and consistency they will hope to reproduce at this level.

They can also draw inspiration from their bronze-medal finish at Uruguay 2018, a reminder that the team has previously enjoyed success at the tournament.

For Morocco, the priority will be to avoid another slow start. For New Zealand, it is about turning strong regional performances into a breakthrough result on the world stage.

Poland vs Nigeria: Flamingos face early Test

Group B | Mohammed VI Football Complex, Pitch 4, Rabat

Nigeria’s Flamingos begin their FIFA U-17 Women’s World Cup campaign against Poland, with both teams looking to establish an early foothold in a competitive Group B.

Poland return to the tournament after missing the previous edition, having recently hosted their first FIFA U-20 Women’s World Cup.

The Europeans booked their place in Morocco with a 2-0 victory over England in a play-off at the UEFA Women’s U-17 Championship, demonstrating their ability to deliver when qualification was on the line.

Nigeria, however, arrive with impressive momentum from the African qualifying campaign.

The Flamingos won all four qualification matches, securing their place at the finals with a perfect record and raising expectations ahead of their opening assignment.

The Nigerian side will also begin a new chapter under head coach Akeem Busari following the end of Bankole Olowookere’s successful three-tournament spell in charge.

Busari’s immediate task will be to carry the team’s qualifying form into the tournament proper, where the standard of opposition and the pressure of competing for a world title will present a different challenge.

Poland’s return gives them a chance to make up for their absence from the previous edition, but Nigeria will be determined to start on the front foot and strengthen their chances of reaching the knockout stage.

For the Flamingos, Saturday’s encounter is more than just an opening fixture. It is their first chance to show that their impressive African qualifying campaign can lay the foundation for another strong run on the world stage.

Four fixtures, one big opening day

The opening day of the FIFA U-17 Women’s World Cup Morocco 2026 brings together established contenders, ambitious debutants and hosts eager to make their presence felt.

Germany and Argentina will kick off their respective campaigns with contrasting levels of tournament experience. At the same time, DPR Korea begin their pursuit of an unprecedented third consecutive title against first-timers Puerto Rico.

Morocco will hope to feed off the energy of the home crowd against New Zealand, while Nigeria’s Flamingos face a crucial early examination against Poland.

With qualification ambitions already at stake, the first day gives every team a chance to set the tone for its campaign. For Nigeria, the mission is clear: turn their impressive qualifying form into a winning start and begin their pursuit of global glory on a positive note.

World.title: FIFA U-17 WWC: Flamingos Coach Busari reveals plan for Poland opener
World.content:
Flamingos head coach Akeem Busari has outlined Nigeria’s tactical approach to their opening FIFA U-17 Women’s World Cup fixture against Poland, identifying the European side’s physical advantage and direct attacking style as key areas his team must manage.

Nigeria’s U-17 women’s national team will begin their Group B campaign on Saturday, with Busari expressing confidence in his players while insisting that the Flamingos are approaching the challenge with respect for their opponents and a clear understanding of what is required to compete at the tournament.

Speaking to journalists ahead of the encounter, the Nigerian coach acknowledged Poland’s experience at the competition, describing the fixture as a valuable test for both teams.

Busari stressed that while every nation arrives at the tournament with ambitions of winning the title, performances on the pitch will ultimately determine which teams emerge as genuine contenders.

“For coming into the tournament all of us are champions but as the tournament goes on,” Busari said during the pre-match press conference.

“We have to separate who is going for and who is winning it. So, we respect all teams and I believe all teams respect Nigeria as well.

“For the Polish side, I think they are a team that parade themselves in the tournament frequently, and they know the terrain, equally like us too.”

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

Despite acknowledging Poland’s experience, Busari believes the contest presents an opportunity for the Flamingos to demonstrate their quality and establish their identity from the opening game.

“So, it is going to be a good test for us. It is going to be a good game. We are going to give a good quality of what we are made up as Flamingos,” he added.

Busari targets Poland’s direct approach with Mid-block strategy

The Flamingos coach also offered insight into Nigeria’s assessment of Poland, pointing to the European team’s height, direct approach and tendency to commit several players into the penalty area when attacking crosses.

According to Busari, Poland’s aerial presence and movement inside the box will require Nigeria to remain organised defensively and avoid allowing their opponents to dictate the contest through their preferred style.

“From what we have watched from them, we could see that they are taller and want to use direct play and they want to run in their numbers in the box for crosses,” he explained.

To counter those strengths, Nigeria intend to deploy a mid-block defensive structure, an approach Busari believes will help the team restrict Poland’s attacking options while creating opportunities to play according to their own philosophy.

The strategy is also expected to allow the Flamingos to build attacks from the back rather than being forced into a game dictated by Poland’s physicality and direct play.

“So, all we need to do is to be on the mid block and we would be able to play our philosophy and play from the back.

“We shared our crosses on the mid and the low, and we drive in more on the angular side,” Busari revealed.

With the tactical preparations completed, the Flamingos will now look to translate their plans into a strong performance when they take on Poland on Saturday.

A positive result would provide Nigeria with an important foundation for their Group B campaign as they pursue qualification for the knockout stage and aim to make another strong impression on the global stage.

World.title: Food Security: Abiodun unveils support package for 10,000 Ogun farmers
World.content:
Ogun State Governor, Dapo Abiodun, has unveiled a comprehensive support package for 10,000 rice and cassava farmers, including subsidised fertilisers, herbicides and improved planting materials, alongside the distribution of 10 tractors, other agricultural equipment and 1,200 Android phones to boost food production and strengthen food security.

Abiodun announced the interventions on Friday at the 2026 World Food Day celebration held at the June 12 Cultural Centre, Abeokuta, with the theme, “Innovate Today, Nourish Tomorrow.”

Under the initiative, 2,000 rice farmers will receive two bags of fertiliser and one bag of urea each, while 8,000 cassava farmers will receive the same quantities of fertiliser and urea, alongside 25 bundles of cassava stems each. The government will also provide three litres of herbicides to each beneficiary rice farmer and 10 litres to each cassava farmer.

The 1,200 Android phones, equipped with applications providing weather information, market prices and guidance on best agricultural practices, are designed to give farmers access to timely information, improve production decisions and strengthen their links to agricultural markets.

The 10 tractors and other equipment are being provided to support farm settlements and farmers’ associations across the state, reinforcing the administration’s drive to expand mechanised farming, reduce production costs and increase agricultural output.

Abiodun said his administration was committed to transforming agriculture into a profitable, technology-driven sector capable of creating jobs, attracting investment and strengthening Ogun State’s contribution to national food security.

“We established the Ogun State Agricultural Land Management Agency (OSALMA) to facilitate access to land and promote a responsible and inclusive framework for land-intensive agricultural investment,” he said.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

The governor disclosed that his administration had completed 28 agricultural projects in the last two years across crop production, aquaculture and poultry, with investments in processing, storage, mechanisation and other critical infrastructure aimed at strengthening the agricultural value chain.

Among the projects, he said, were solar dryers, warehouses, cassava processing centres and a poultry processing plant at Ajegunle Farm Settlement in Odeda Local Government Area. The poultry facility has the capacity to process 5,000 birds daily, equivalent to approximately 1.3 million birds annually.

He added that the state had procured 39 tractors, four self-propelled harvesters and other agricultural equipment to improve mechanisation and reduce the burden of manual farming.

On youth empowerment, Abiodun disclosed that more than 200 young people had recently received training in soilless farming through a partnership with Soilless Farm Lab, with start-up support provided to help beneficiaries establish their own agricultural enterprises.

He said the administration’s objective was to expand local processing, retain greater value within the state’s economy and create employment opportunities across the agricultural value chain.

“Our goal is to process more locally, retain greater value and create more jobs. We seek partnerships that create jobs, transfer knowledge, empower farmers and develop local capacity,” he said.

The governor called on investors to take advantage of opportunities in commercial farming, agro-processing, livestock production, aquaculture, mechanisation, irrigation, storage and cold-chain facilities, assuring them of the state’s readiness to support responsible agricultural investments.

He said the administration was working towards an agricultural economy in which farming was profitable, agribusinesses thrived and rural communities prospered.

Abiodun also highlighted the Ogun State Farmer Information Management System, launched in April 2023, which has captured more than 160,000 farmers and agricultural value-chain actors.

He explained that the platform was designed to support evidence-based policymaking, improve the targeting of agricultural interventions and ensure that government assistance reached intended beneficiaries.

“Under the Ogun State Economic Transformation Project (OGSTEP), agribusiness firms purchased over 283,000 tonnes of agricultural produce.

“Farmers organised into clusters also received capacity-building support and connections to off-takers. These measures have helped turn increased production into dependable income,” he said.

The governor commended President Bola Ahmed Tinubu for efforts to strengthen local fertiliser production and improve farmers’ access to essential agricultural inputs. He also acknowledged the contributions of the First Lady, Senator Oluremi Tinubu, to initiatives supporting women farmers.

He said the Ogun State Government would continue to complement federal agricultural initiatives through targeted support for farmers, responsible investment and stronger market linkages.

Earlier, the Commissioner for Agriculture and Food Security, Bolu Owotomo, described World Food Day as a reminder that access to nutritious and affordable food was fundamental to human dignity and sustainable development.

He said innovation was essential to building a resilient food system and called for greater investment in women and young people through improved access to land, finance, training, technology and viable agribusiness opportunities.

Owotomo disclosed that more than 12,000 farmers had benefited from training and agricultural inputs under OGSTEP.

He said the latest interventions focused on three areas: digital empowerment through the distribution of Android phones; mechanisation support through agricultural equipment; and subsidised inputs for 2,000 rice farmers and 8,000 cassava farmers.

According to him, the input support operates under an arrangement in which beneficiaries contribute 30 per cent of the cost, depending on the category, while the government covers the remaining 70 per cent through its partnership with the International Fund for Agricultural Development (IFAD).

In his keynote address, a former Deputy Vice-Chancellor of the Federal University of Agriculture, Abeokuta, Professor Kolawole Adebayo, said Ogun State occupied a strategic position in the future of Nigeria’s food system because of its agricultural potential and proximity to major consumer markets.

He noted that the state’s 1.2 million hectares of arable land offered significant opportunities for agro-industrial investment, stressing the need for forward-looking policies and sustained commitment to innovations that would deliver lasting benefits to the food system.

Adebayo called for an integrated transportation network linking rail, road, water and air transport to facilitate the efficient movement of agricultural produce, preserve quality and reduce post-harvest losses.

He commended the state government for developing agro-industrial processing zones, improving land-clearing services for smallholder farmers and expanding access to agricultural inputs.

He also identified the Farmer Information Management System and the establishment of the Nigerian Food Bank in Ogun State as initiatives that could strengthen the state’s contribution to national food security.

The National Programme Coordinator of the Special Agro-Industrial Processing Zones Programme, Dr Kabiru Yusuf, represented by the National Agriculture Expert, Dr Louis Enaberue, commended Abiodun for his support for the agricultural sector and urged beneficiaries to make effective use of the equipment and farm inputs.

Similarly, the South-West Coordinator of the Commodity Farmers Association of Nigeria, Segun Dasaolu, acknowledged the state government’s interventions, saying they were helping to strengthen agricultural development and support farmers across the region.

Speaking on behalf of farm settlers across the state, Rotimi Sogunle thanked the governor for supporting farming communities and described OGSTEP as a significant intervention in the state’s agricultural sector.

The highlight of the celebration was the symbolic presentation of tractors, agricultural equipment, Android phones, fertilisers, herbicides and other farm inputs to beneficiaries.

World.title: The cost of the gospel: A story that should humble every generation (1), By Ayo Akerele
World.content:
In July 1986, Dr Billy Graham made a remarkable and costly investment, committing millions of dollars to host a landmark international conference in Amsterdam, Netherlands. The gathering brought together eight thousand pastors and evangelists drawn from remote villages across Central Africa and from virtually every inhabited corner of the earth. Delegates from more than 180 nations were in attendance, representing one of the most diverse gatherings of gospel ministers the world had ever witnessed. In an extraordinary act of personal generosity, Dr Graham personally sponsored the flights and hotel accommodations of every delegate, ensuring that no one who was called to be there would be prevented from attending by the weight of financial hardship. It was not merely a conference, it was a statement of how seriously one man took the advance of the gospel to the ends of the earth.

Among those who made the journey was an evangelist from a small, obscure village in Central Africa, a man named Joseph. Throughout the conference sessions, Joseph sat in complete and rapt attention, absorbing every word that Dr Graham shared from the platform. Before the conference drew to a close, Joseph made a quiet but earnest request: a private audience with Dr Graham himself. That request was graciously and humbly granted.

When the two men finally sat together, Joseph began to share his story. What Dr Graham heard in that room that day would remain with him for the rest of his life.

In Joseph’s own words: “As a young man, I heard the gospel on a dusty African road, and I responded immediately, trusting Jesus Christ as my Lord and Saviour. The moment I believed, an overwhelming longing took hold of me, a burning desire to return to my native village and share the good news of the Kingdom of Heaven with my own people. I went from door to door, telling everyone I encountered what had happened to me, fully expecting their faces to light up with the same joy that had flooded my own heart. Instead, I was met with fury and rage.

The men of the village seized me and pinned me to the ground, while the women flogged me mercilessly with barbed wire. When it was over, I was dragged into the surrounding bush and abandoned there to die. I crawled on my hands and knees to a nearby watering hole, and over the course of several days I slowly began to recover. In those long, painful hours of solitude and reflection, I convinced myself that I must have left something essential out of the message, or perhaps I had communicated it poorly. So I rehearsed my testimony carefully, prayed with every ounce of fervour I could gather, and eventually limped back to the village to try again.

I received another flogging. When I had recovered sufficiently to stand once more, I returned a third time, and was whipped a third time. The barbed wire found the same wounds that had barely begun to heal, tearing them open afresh. But something was unmistakably different on that third visit. As I began to lose consciousness and the world around me faded, I noticed something I had not seen before: one of the women who had been beating me had suddenly stopped. She was weeping openly. And then I saw others beginning to weep alongside her. I awoke in my own bed, being tenderly cared for by the very hands that had previously sought to destroy me.

By the grace of Almighty God, and through that patient and suffering witness, the entire village turned to Christ.”

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

It is recorded by Dr David Jeremiah that at this precise point in the conversation, Joseph quietly lifted his shirt to reveal the scars permanently etched across his chest and back, a living testimony written not in ink, but in flesh and blood. Dr. Graham was visibly shaken and deeply moved. Later, speaking privately to members of his own staff, the great evangelist uttered words that deserve to reverberate in the ears of every minister of the gospel alive today:

“I am not fit to untie his shoes, and he wanted to meet me?”

This story places before us a piercing and deeply uncomfortable challenge: we must stop cheapening the gospel.

A man endured unimaginable and repeated suffering, returning not once, not twice, but three times to the source of his torment, to proclaim the very same gospel that many preachers and church leaders today dilute, negotiate away, or quietly set aside in pursuit of fame, financial security, and institutional influence. Dr Erwin Lutzer once issued a devastating indictment to the contemporary Church:

“Many of us are not even willing to live for Jesus, much less die for Him.”

Those words carry crushing weight when placed alongside the image of Joseph’s scars. The fire of genuine, heaven-sent revival must fall upon the Church once more. The gospel has never been without cost, it cost Jesus Christ His precious blood, and it has cost countless faithful believers throughout the centuries their livelihoods, their families, their freedom, and their very lives.

I am personally drawn to stories of unwavering, costly faith, testimonies of men and women who planted their feet and refused to move regardless of what it cost them. These testimonies do not merely inspire us. They leave our generation without excuse. If Billy Graham, one of the most widely recognised and celebrated evangelists of the twentieth century, could be brought to a posture of profound humility before the sacrifice of one unknown African pastor, then so should every one of us who dares to call ourselves a minister of Christ.

But let us press this question even further. Pastor Joseph was a young man when these events took place. Do we still have young men and women in the Church today who carry that same rare and burning commitment to the cause of the gospel? Is the current generation of Christian youth genuinely equipped, willing, and spiritually capable of carrying forward and sustaining the fire of the truth of the gospel?

“And there arose another generation after them, which knew not the Lord.” (Judges 2:10)

This passage haunts me. It reminds me of a story I encountered not long ago, the children of an elderly man of God who were weeping bitterly as they watched their father suffer at the hands of the very church he had faithfully served for decades. These children openly expressed their regrets, confessing that they wished the hands of time could be pulled back so they might reconsider their decision to follow Jesus, and particularly to follow the local church their father had led them into. But it was too late.

Their lives had been deeply wounded by the very leader they had so dearly cherished, damaged in ways that would require nothing short of a unique and extraordinary dimension of God’s mercy to heal. They had been shown a distorted and false version of the true God of the Bible. They had been sold a counterfeit Jesus, another Jesus altogether, not the love-embodying, self-sacrificing Son of God, the true and living Jesus of the Scriptures.

The tragic reality is that those children may never serve the God of their father, much less contemplate dying for Him in the manner of Pastor Joseph.

Such is the heartbreaking condition of tens of thousands of young people in churches today who stand on the very precipice of apostasy and, in some cases, outright atheism. Some totter at the edge of a complete rejection of Jesus and the Christian faith, having been disillusioned and embittered by the rank hypocrisy they have witnessed among those who claimed to represent Him. Others who still call themselves Christians lead lives that bear little meaningful resemblance to what authentic, New Testament Christianity actually looks like. The majority of our young people are spiritually fireless and entirely passionless.

They are in church but are rarely in Christ. They can organise grand programmes but can rarely agonise in genuine prayer. They can pay for anything but can rarely pray about anything. They can feast lavishly but can rarely fast sincerely. They can sow seed offerings into anything but can rarely grow spiritually into anything. If the fathers of this generation do not urgently congregate a solemn assembly to repair the broken walls of the gospel, the youths of today, already standing at the precipice, will tumble headlong into brazen apostasy, and the influence of the Church will be obliterated with reckless speed. Dr Erwin Lutzer once said, “the fall of Turkey into the hands of radical islamists proves that there is no guarantee that the church will always survive in every nation.”

“Now the sons of Eli were corrupt; they did not know the Lord.” (1 Samuel 2:12).

The fathers are ageing. The children are aching. The world is growing hotter in its hostility to truth. God’s devoted lovers are thinning out. Culture seems increasingly to be prevailing over Scripture rather than being shaped by it. Post-modernism and relativism are now aggressively displacing absolute truth in the public square. Society is rapidly losing its tolerance for authentic, Bible-believing Christians, a trajectory that mirrors John J Murray’s sober observation: “We have now gone back to the era of the early apostles. The Roman empire under which many Christians were martyred was pluralistic and supremely tolerant of religion. The only people they could not tolerate were the Christians.”

Persecution of faithful Christians has more than doubled around the world and will yet multiply in the years ahead. The future of the Church in Africa, and indeed globally, now rests to a significant degree in the hands of the Christian young people of today. But the question that must keep every spiritual leader awake at night is this: will the youths of today, who are drinking from the wells dug by the fathers, take up their own swords and sharpen them for the battle ahead? To be continued.

Ayo Akerele is the senior pastor of Rhema Assembly and the founder of the Voice of the Watchmen Ministries in Ontario, Canada. He can be reached through [email protected]. You can connect with him on: YouTube: @VoiceoftheWatchmen, TikTok: @drayoakerele, Instagram: @drayoakerele, Facebook: @Ayo Akerele

World.title: Maina’s son, Faisal, arrested after six years on the run – Report
World.content:
Fugitive Faisal Maina, son of ex-convict Abdulrasheed Maina, former chairman of the defunct Pension Reform Task Team (PRTT), has reportedly been arrested, six years after jumping bail.

TheCable reports that the State Security Service (SSS, also known as DSS) arrested Faisal and handed him over to the Economic and Financial Crimes Commission (EFCC).

He was reportedly arrested following intelligence indicating that he had secretly returned to Nigeria.

“His arrest followed credible intelligence which indicated that Faisal had secretly returned to the country,” a source told the publication.

According to the paper, SSS operatives tracked and arrested Faisal in the Karsana area of Abuja before transferring him to the EFCC.

Faisal has been on the run since 2020, after the EFCC arraigned him on three counts bordering on money laundering.

Although he was granted bail, he breached his bail conditions and fled the country.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

Both the SSS media unit and the EFCC spokesperson have not responded to PREMIUM TIMES’ requests for comment on the matter.

PREMIUM TIMES will provide more updates in subsequent reports.

Background

Faisal’s trial continued in his absence and culminated in his conviction by the Federal High Court in Abuja in October 2021. The court sentenced him to 14 years’ imprisonment on money laundering charges.

The trial judge, Okong Abang, held that the EFCC established that Faisal operated a fictitious United Bank for Africa (UBA) account through which his father allegedly laundered N58.1 million.

According to the court, the funds were deposited into an account operated in the name of “Alhaji Faisal Farm 2” and subsequently withdrawn by Faisal and his father between October 2013 and June 2019.

In November 2022, the Court of Appeal upheld Faisal’s conviction but reduced his sentence from 14 years to seven years. The appellate court held that the trial court should not have imposed the maximum sentence on a first-time offender.

His father, Mr Maina, served an eight-year prison sentence at the Kuje Correctional Centre in Abuja for laundering N2 billion in pension funds.

He was released earlier this year, but has since been declared wanted over an alleged case of receiving stolen property.

World.title: NSIB kicks off probe into aircraft door loss incident
World.content:
The Nigerian Safety Investigation Bureau (NSIB) has begun an investigation into an incident involving a foreign-registered aircraft operated by Triton Aviation after the airline’s crew reported that a door of the aircraft opened mid-air shortly after taking off from Abuja on Thursday.

The Challenger 604 aircraft, with registration number T7-SEI, departed the Nnamdi Azikiwe International Airport on Thursday for Lagos.

It was about three nautical miles from the airport, climbing through 3,500 feet, when its crew declared a Mayday emergency, according to the NSIB.

The aircraft returned to Abuja and landed safely on Runway 22 at 16:34 Coordinated Universal Time (UTC), with nine people on board, comprising three crew members and six passengers.

In a statement issued Friday and signed by its director-general and CEO, Alex Badeh Jr., the NSIB said it recovered the missing door and secured it at its wreckage hangar.

“The bureau has commenced its investigation to establish the circumstances surrounding the occurrence,” the statement said.

PREMIUM TIMES earlier reported that the aircraft’s crew declared a Mayday emergency after reporting that a door had opened during flight shortly after take-off.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

Airport fire, rescue personnel and medical teams were placed on standby while air traffic controllers directed the aircraft back to Abuja.

The aircraft landed safely, and the air traffic controller subsequently observed that the door was missing from the fuselage.

A video circulating on social media also appears to show the missing door. In the footage, an unidentified man said farmers had found the object while returning from their farm in the Abuja area.

The NSIB said its investigation will establish the circumstances surrounding the incident, including what caused the door to detach and the sequence of events during the flight.

The aircraft is registered in San Marino, a small European country surrounded by Italy, according to the NSIB statement.

The bureau said it will provide further updates as the investigation progresses.

World.title: Ebola: Kenya records third case, continues contact tracing
World.content:
Kenya has confirmed a third case of Ebola after a 65-year-old woman tested positive while in quarantine.

The woman is a close relative of Kenya’s first confirmed patient, a 40-year-old who died from Ebola on 5 October, two days after arriving in Kenya from the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC).

The Associated Press (AP) reported that the woman had been in quarantine since 6 October and developed symptoms before testing positive. She has since been transferred to an infectious disease unit for treatment.

The second patient, a 39-year-old man from the same family, remains stable, according to Kenya’s Ministry of Health.

The ministry said there was no evidence of community transmission, as all three cases were linked to the first patient and the individuals had been in quarantine.

Nigeria’s preparedness

The development comes as Nigeria continues to monitor the regional outbreak and strengthen preparedness against possible importation of the virus.

PREMIUM TIMES reported on 7 October that the Nigeria Centre for Disease Control and Prevention (NCDC) was reviewing the country’s preparedness after Kenya confirmed its first imported case of the Bundibugyo strain of Ebola.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

In a statement issued on 6 October, the NCDC said the case highlighted the risk of international importation through travel and population movement, including the possibility of the virus entering Nigeria.

The agency said it was working with the Federal Ministry of Health and Social Welfare, Port Health Services, state governments and other partners to strengthen surveillance, early detection, laboratory diagnosis, isolation, contact tracing and infection prevention.

It also said Nigeria conducted a national Ebola preparedness simulation exercise to assess its readiness to respond to a possible case.

As of 6 October, the NCDC said Nigeria had no confirmed Ebola case.

Contact tracing continues

Kenya’s first case involved a 40-year-old man who had been living in the DRC and travelled through Uganda before arriving in Nairobi. He tested positive for Ebola and died on 5 October.

The confirmation of a second case on 14 October raised concerns about further infections among people exposed to the initial patient.

PREMIUM TIMES reported on 14 October that the second patient, a 39-year-old close relative of the first case, developed symptoms while in quarantine.

At the time, Kenyan authorities had identified 128 contacts linked to the first patient, with 113 located and efforts ongoing to trace the remaining 15.

In its report on Friday, AP said three contacts of the initial patient remained unaccounted for, while authorities continued efforts to trace people who might have been exposed.

The latest case brings the number of confirmed Ebola infections in Kenya to three.

Regional outbreak

The cases in Kenya are linked to the ongoing Ebola outbreak in the DRC, where the Bundibugyo virus has caused thousands of infections and deaths.

The World Health Organisation (WHO) said the DRC had recorded 7,890 confirmed cases and 3,799 deaths as of 23 September.

The outbreak has raised concerns about cross-border transmission, particularly as people travel between affected areas and neighbouring countries.

The Bundibugyo virus is a distinct species of Ebola virus. No vaccine or treatment has been specifically approved for this strain.

World.title: World Bank’s $5.79 billion financing will boost ongoing business expansion efforts – Tinubu
World.content:
President Bola Tinubu has said the World Bank Group’s decision to mobilise about $5.79 billion in private financing for Nigeria will boost ongoing business expansion efforts and help attract investment to the economy.

The president hailed the World Bank’s push in an X post on Friday, noting that Nigeria has introduced economic reforms to build a stronger foundation for investment and give more Nigerians the opportunity to earn better livelihoods.

“I welcome the World Bank Group’s work to mobilise up to $5.79 billion in private financing for Nigeria. This partnership supports our efforts to help businesses expand and attract investment into agriculture and digital infrastructure,” Mr Tinubu said.

The World Bank Group disclosed the financing target in a report published on Sunday, saying that the fund is designed for farmers trying to secure quality seed before the planting season, small business owners unable to obtain affordable credit and students struggling to connect to digital classrooms.

The Bretton Woods institutions said the fund will also aid Project BRIDGE and help the country use a public-private partnership to build, own, and operate a nationwide open-access fibre-optic network.

Project BRIDGE is a Federal Government project aiming to deploy 90,000 kilometres of new fibre-optic infrastructure across Nigeria and expand nationwide digital connectivity.

By combining policy reform, investment platforms, risk mitigation, and commercial financing, the bank said it is channelling private capital towards sectors critical to Nigeria’s growth and economic transformation.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

The $5.79 billion initiative is designed to mobilise private investment through a mix of World Bank-supported programmes, financing from the International Finance Corporation and risk-mitigation instruments provided by the Multilateral Investment Guarantee Agency.

The project is also expected to attract at least $156 million in private equity in its first investor-selection round, with subsequent financing potentially unlocking up to $1.1 billion in private investment by 2030.

In his remarks on Friday, Mr Tinubu said Nigeria has gone a step further by assembling a pipeline of 65 bankable projects seeking $78.5 billion in investment.

He said Minister of Finance and Coordinating Minister of the Economy Taiwo Oyedele presented the opportunities alongside Central Bank of Nigeria Governor Olayemi Cardoso at the Nigeria Investors Forum on the sidelines of the 2026 IMF-World Bank Annual Meetings in Bangkok.

“I invite Nigerian and international investors to examine these projects and engage directly with their sponsors through Projects Nigeria,” the president said.

Mr Tinubu added that his administration will work with investors and Nigerians to resolve obstacles and drive viable investments into execution, creating jobs and expanding opportunities for Nigerians.

World.title: Iran denies Saudi accusation of involvement in Houthi attacks
World.content:
Iran President Masoud Pezeshkian

Iran on Friday denied having anything to do with attacks by Yemen’s Houthis, a day after Saudi Arabia accused it of having encouraged the group’s recent escalation against the kingdom.

Since Yemen’s civil war flared back to life in July, the pro-Iran Houthis have repeatedly struck Saudi targets including Red Sea tankers, oil facilities and Riyadh’s international airport, where 13 people were killed in a single attack last week.

A Saudi-led military coalition has supported Yemen’s internationally recognised government for more than a decade, and reported on Friday having intercepted more missiles and drones as the kingdom comes under sustained attack from the Houthis.

A day earlier, a Saudi foreign ministry official said Iran had “encouraged” the escalation, which Tehran denied.

“The Islamic Republic of Iran rejects any claim that Iran has played a role in Yemeni (Houthi) operations,” Iranian foreign ministry spokesman Esmaeil Baqaei said in a statement.

“Yemen’s armed forces act according to their own interests and assessments, and such claims are not credible to those familiar with relations between Iran and its friends. Nevertheless, Iran does not consider an escalation of tensions to be in the interests of any party,” he added.

The Saudi official, deputy minister for public diplomacy Dr. Rayed Krimly, had said the Houthis rejected an offer to meet in Oman at the outset of the latest round of hostilities.

Baqaei however reiterated an offer to mediate between the two sides, saying Tehran “has always been ready to use its good offices to help end the hostilities”.

On Friday, a spokesman for the Saudi-led military coalition said it had “intercepted and destroyed three drones in the southern area and Riyadh… and two cruise missiles over the Red Sea”.

He added that “in the past hours, we intercepted and destroyed a ballistic missile over Yanbu”, a city home to the terminus of a major oil pipeline on the Red Sea coast.

The Houthi attacks have proliferated since the group launched a lightning offensive in Yemen in September, seizing strategic government-held territory along the Red Sea coast overlooking a major chokepoint for global shipping.

The pressure on Saudi Arabia, the world’s largest oil exporter, comes as global energy markets were already rattled by Iran’s closure of the Strait of Hormuz at the outset of the wider Middle East war in February.

– Airport struck –

Yemeni government forces have launched a counteroffensive with Saudi air support to retake areas seized by the Houthis, but have so far failed to reverse their gains.

On Friday, the local security office in Aden, the government’s interim capital, said two missiles landed within the perimeter of the city’s airport, “in the second incident of its kind in less than a week”, adding that no one was killed.

The Houthis, in a statement attributed to a military source, said the attack targeted “the Saudi forces’ command headquarters” as well as a weapons depot.

The Yemeni information ministry said in a statement that a Yemenia Airways flight from Aden to Cairo narrowly missed being struck.

It was “preparing for takeoff at the very moment when the terrorist Houthi militia targeted the airport with two missiles that landed approximately 500 metres from the aircraft and about 100 metres from the centre of the runway,” a statement said.

“What occurred was not merely an assault on a civilian airport, but a direct threat to the lives of passengers and flight crews, to aviation safety, and a grave violation of international laws and norms.”

The day before, the group launched a deadly missile attack on the presidential palace in Aden, killing five people and wounding 16 others, according to the health minister.

Yemeni Prime Minister Shaya al-Zindani denounced the “cowardly” act on X, calling it a “continuation of (the Houthis’) criminal pattern”.

A government minister said on condition of anonymity that the Houthis hit command centres for Yemeni and Saudi coalition forces housed at the palace complex.

Media affiliated with the Houthis said the attack had targeted “the headquarters of military operations, led by Saudi officers, at the Al-Maashiq Palace in Aden”.

AFP

World.title: Anthropic proposes law regulating AI to US lawmakers
World.content:
File image

Anthropic, the creator of the AI assistant Claude, confirmed on Friday it is circulating a draft bill among US lawmakers aimed at regulating artificial intelligence to address the lack of federal legislation on the risks posed by the new technology.

According to the draft, first reported by Politico on Friday, Washington could block a model’s release or use if there is an imminent risk of killing or seriously injuring more than 50 people, or causing more than $1 billion in damages, but only with a judge’s approval.

A company spokesperson told AFP that the proposal “grants the federal government the ability to block or deter dangerous deployments of the most powerful models.”

“It requires frontier developers to test the most powerful models, be transparent to the public about their findings, submit them to independent evaluation, and maintain a robust security program,” the spokesperson said.

AI policy in the United States under President Donald Trump has relied primarily on voluntary industry pledges and executive orders intended to sustain an AI boom that tech leaders say is driving the country’s economy.

Congress, politically divided and heavily lobbied by Big Tech, has yet to pass a federal AI law, and is out of session until after next month’s midterm elections.

Security became a hot topic after recent revelations of security incidents caused by AI agents — autonomous software that operates without constant human supervision — that escaped the control of their developers.

Anthropic, which was banned from the Pentagon by the Trump administration in February, was forced by Washington in June to suspend its most advanced models for nearly three weeks.

Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei called on the industry last month to slow down development, fearing that a group of AI agents could take control of “the entire internet” within six to 12 months.
