World.title: Chile Answers Bolivia Sea Claim on 16 Oct
World.content:
Guards outside the Palacio de Gobierno in La Paz, Bolivia, in October 2022 (Photo: Yastay, CC BY-SA 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons)

CHILE · DIPLOMACY

Key Facts — The country Bolivia is a landlocked Andean nation and Chile is its Pacific neighbour, whose ports Bolivian cargo uses under a free-transit regime.

— Why it matters The Bolivia sea claim is the oldest dispute between the two, and it shapes cargo, fuel and mining deals that US investors watch.

— Why now Chilean President José Antonio Kast made the first official visit by a Chilean head of state to La Paz since 1955.

— What happened On Friday 16 October, Bolivia’s Rodrigo Paz called the claim “permanent and irrenounceable”, and Kast said some claims are settled by courts.

— The numbers The joint declaration has 21 points, and none of them names the sea question.

— What it means for you The sea dispute does not block trade, transit or mining talks, so cargo and energy plans continue, but a clash over the claim could slow them.

— Still open Whether the new political consultations will ever take up sea access, and when the free-transit group meets in La Paz.

— Power Index Chile ranks 3rd of 14 in Chile ranks 3rd of 14 in The Rio Times Latin America Power Index , with 63.6 points (October 2026 edition). Bolivia ranks 12th of 14 in The Rio Times Latin America Power Index , with 28.4 points (October 2026 edition).

Bolivia’s President Rodrigo Paz told Chile’s José Antonio Kast on Friday 16 October that the Bolivia sea claim is a “permanent and irrenounceable” objective, Red Uno reports. Kast answered at a press conference that each nation has its claims and that some are settled by courts.

For US readers, the exchange matters because Bolivian cargo, fuel and minerals move through Chilean Pacific ports, and the two governments are trying to build on that trade. The sea question is the main political risk to that thaw.

What Paz Said on the Bolivia Sea Claim

Paz spoke after meeting Kast and signing the bilateral instruments, Red Uno reports. He said, in our translation, “the maritime claim is a permanent and irrenounceable objective” and “a constitutional mandate”.

Latin America Power Index · October 2026 edition Bolivia ranks 12th of 14 with 28.4 points. Strongest pillar: military means (55); weakest: diplomatic & cultural influence (13). Alignment group: Hedging. WatchRating below investment grade (CCC+); economy contracting (-1.2%); inflation of 20%. See the full index, the business lens and the data →

He added that “Bolivia does not renounce its history, its rights or dialogue”. Paz said history should not anchor Bolivia’s development, and that the future will be a priority for his government.

He also said that about half a million Bolivians live in or move through Chile, Red Uno reports. Paz called this a “diplomacy of the people” that moves faster than the states.

Paz, Bolivia’s president, is profiled in Rodrigo Paz Pereira Profile: The Bolivian Facing Kast. At home he faces critics such as former president Evo Morales, who said on Thursday 15 October that failing to negotiate the sea at the meeting would be “treason to the homeland”, Opinión reported.

The summary of the accords that Paz posted on his own account did not mention the sea claim, El Deber reported on Friday evening. It ended with the line that Bolivia does not renounce its history or its rights, and that it thinks of its future.

What Kast Answered in La Paz

Kast, Chile’s conservative president, spoke to Chilean media at his country’s consulate in La Paz, Red Uno reports. Asked how the Bolivian claim to a sovereign outlet on the Pacific fits the new rapprochement, he first spoke of legitimate differences.

“Both presidents noted that legitimate differences exist between our countries’ positions, but that cannot stop development, progress and looking after people,” he said, in our translation. Red Uno adds that Kast did not raise any specific negotiation on maritime sovereignty.

Asked a second time about the sea outlet, Kast said, “Legitimately, each nation has its claims.” He added, “Some of them are settled by various courts, which does not prevent a country from holding certain historical milestones in its legislation.”

Red Uno, El Deber and Chile’s Emol carried the same words. El Deber read them as Kast saying that the maritime claim was settled by international tribunals, a reading that his full sentence does not state.

Kast then listed what the differences should not stop, in Red Uno’s account: tourism, trade and joint action against drug trafficking, organised crime and smuggling. In his speech earlier that day he had said Bolivia has its positions and Chile has its own, El Deber reports.

What the Joint Declaration Says and Leaves Out

Chile’s Foreign Ministry published the joint declaration signed by both presidents on 16 October. It has 21 numbered points, and the text does not name the maritime claim or sovereign access to the sea.

Point 4 says that, despite the differences that have marked their history, dialogue, mutual respect and cooperation should guide relations, based on respect for international law. It asks the Political Consultations Mechanism to handle all topics of mutual interest.

El Deber reads that wording as an allusion to the 2018 court ruling, and says it lets the two sides keep talking within international law. The declaration itself does not mention the court, so that reading is the newspaper’s.

Point 3 revives that mechanism, along with the cultural and education commission, the drugs commission, the follow-up body for the ATIT transit agreement and the free-transit working group. Point 13 reaffirms Bolivia’s free transit through Chilean territory and ports under existing agreements.

The 14th meeting of that working group is to take place in La Paz, the text says, with cargo to and from overseas through Chilean ports on its agenda. The declaration gives no date for it.

The declaration also welcomes progress on the Sica Sica to Arica oil pipeline reversal and a fibre-optic corridor between the two countries. It closes with Kast’s invitation for Paz to make an official visit to Chile in 2027, which Paz accepted.

The five instruments signed that day are set out in Kast and Paz Sign Five Chile Bolivia Accords. The earlier build-up is covered in Kast Meets Rodrigo Paz in Bolivia Friday.

The Court Ruling Behind the Wording

Bolivia lost its coastline to Chile in the War of the Pacific in the late 19th century, and the claim to regain a route to the sea has lasted since. The background is explained in Chile Bolivia Relations: Kast Visit Explained.

The International Court of Justice, the UN’s highest court, heard Bolivia’s case on the obligation to negotiate access to the Pacific Ocean. It delivered its judgment on the merits on 1 October 2018, according to the court’s website.

The court concluded that none of the legal bases Bolivia invoked established an obligation for Chile to negotiate sovereign access to the Pacific, its case page says. Kast’s remark about disputes “settled by various courts” fits that history, though he did not name the case.

Jaime Aparicio, a former diplomat, told El Deber that the 2018 ruling means no pending maritime issue remains in legal terms. He blamed Morales for taking the case to The Hague, which is his opinion and not a finding.

What It Means for You

Chile is a Pacific export hub for Bolivian cargo, so the free-transit talks and port logistics in the declaration affect importers, miners and fuel traders. US firms with Andean supply chains should watch whether the La Paz transit meeting is scheduled.

The two presidents showed that a dispute about territory need not block practical deals on trade, minerals and energy. A flare-up over the claim, for example at a Bolivian political rally, would be a risk to that pace, though no such move has been announced.

Travellers face no change from these statements, and entry and border rules were not altered in the texts reviewed. For wider context on how power is organised in Santiago, see Chile Politics Explained, Who Holds Power in 2026.

What Is Not Known

It is not known whether the Political Consultations Mechanism will ever take up sea access, because the declaration gives it “all topics of mutual interest” without naming one. Neither government has said that the topic is closed or open for talks.

The sources reviewed do not show whether Kast meant any particular court ruling, since he named none. Chile’s government has not published its own text of the press conference, so the quotes come from Bolivian outlets and from Emol, in our translation.

No date has been published for the free-transit meeting in La Paz, or for Paz’s visit to Chile in 2027. The declaration does not say whether ambassadors will return, although Kast said in his speech that the political consultations will work step by step toward restoring relations at the highest diplomatic level, La Tercera reports.

Reaction from Chilean lawmakers and from Morales to Kast’s answer had not been found when this was written. Paz’s office has not said whether he will answer Aparicio’s criticism or Morales’s earlier warning.

Frequently Asked Questions

What did Paz say about the Bolivia sea claim?

Paz said on 16 October that the maritime claim is a permanent and irrenounceable objective and a constitutional mandate. He added that Bolivia does not renounce its history, its rights or dialogue.

What did Kast answer on the sea claim?

Kast said each nation legitimately has its claims and that some are settled by various courts. Red Uno says he did not raise any specific negotiation on maritime sovereignty.

Does the Chile Bolivia declaration mention the sea?

The 21-point declaration published by Chile’s Foreign Ministry does not name the maritime claim. Point 4 refers to dialogue and respect for international law, and gives the political consultations body all topics of mutual interest.

What did the ICJ decide in 2018?

The International Court of Justice delivered its judgment on Bolivia’s case against Chile on 1 October 2018. It found that none of the legal bases Bolivia invoked created an obligation for Chile to negotiate sovereign access to the Pacific, and said the two countries may continue their dialogue.

When will Paz visit Chile?

Kast invited Paz to make an official visit to Chile in 2027, and the declaration says Paz accepted. No date has been published.

World.title: Peru Cites Lowest Inflation, Lima at 4.55%
World.content:
Stalls at the entrance of Market No. 1 in Surquillo, Lima (file photo, 2014). (Photo: Chuck Moravec, CC BY 2.0, via Wikimedia Commons)

PERU · INFLATION

Key Facts — The country Peru is one of the world’s main copper and gold exporters, and its central bank has used an explicit inflation target since 2001, with Julio Velarde as its president for almost 20 years.

— Why it matters Velarde says Peru has had the lowest inflation in Latin America this century, a claim that US investors in Peruvian bonds, the sol and mining will weigh against current prices.

— Why now He made the claim at an International Monetary Fund and World Bank seminar in Bangkok, in remarks carried on Friday 16 October, while Lima inflation sits above target.

— What happened On 16 October Velarde said Peru’s core inflation has stayed below US inflation this century and that dollar loans fell from 81% of bank credit in 2000 to 23% now.

— The numbers Lima prices rose 4.55% in the 12 months to September, above the 1% to 3% target, against 3.7% for US consumer prices in the same month.

— What it means for you US investors, importers of Peruvian copper, fruit and fishmeal, and travellers in Lima should treat the century record as history, not a forecast.

— Still open Which countries and which inflation measure Velarde compared, and whether Lima inflation returns to the 1% to 3% range in 2027 as the bank projects.

— Power Index Peru ranks 5th of 14 in Peru ranks 5th of 14 in The Rio Times Latin America Power Index , with 54.7 points (October 2026 edition).

Peru has had the lowest inflation in Latin America this century, central bank president Julio Velarde said at a seminar in Bangkok, reported on Friday 16 October. He spoke during the International Monetary Fund (IMF) and World Bank annual meetings, and the Peruvian outlets Infobae and Gestión carried his remarks.

For US readers the claim matters because Peru is one of the world’s main copper and gold exporters, and US investors watch its currency and bonds. It also needs a caveat, because Lima’s prices rose 4.55% in the year to September, above both the bank’s target and the US rate of 3.7%.

What Julio Velarde Said in Bangkok

Velarde spoke at a seminar called “Pathways to Resilience: Success Stories in Reform and Partnership”, moderated by IMF deputy managing director Nigel Clarke. Officials from Portugal, Papua New Guinea and Rwanda also took part, Infobae reported.

Latin America Power Index · October 2026 edition Peru ranks 5th of 14 with 54.7 points. Strongest pillar: military means (71); weakest: future resources (37). Alignment group: Closer to Washington. See the full index, the business lens and the data →

He said Peru has recorded the lowest inflation in the region so far this century, Gestión reported. He added that Peru’s core inflation, which strips out volatile items such as food and energy, has stayed below US inflation in this century.

He credited the central bank’s autonomy, set in its 1992 organic law, which bars it from financing the government or state development banks and from running multiple exchange rates. Peru was also the first Latin American country to adopt a flexible exchange rate, he said, and it began explicit inflation targets in 2001.

Velarde said the hyperinflation of the late 1980s pushed Peruvians into dollars, so the bank first had to hold inflation near the US level. It then asked that prices also be shown in soles and set reserve requirements that cut the dollar share of bank loans from 81% in 2000 to 23% today.

Is It Really the Lowest Inflation in Latin America?

Velarde has made this claim before, including at a Lima city hall ceremony reported on 15 July and at an awards event reported on 2 September. At the September event he put Peru’s average annual inflation at 3.2% over two decades, América TV reported.

We checked the claim against World Bank annual consumer price data for 2001 to 2025, for the 17 Spanish-, Portuguese- and French-speaking Latin American countries with a complete series. Peru’s simple average annual rate was 3.0%, below Chile at 3.8%, Mexico at 4.5%, Colombia at 5.2% and Brazil at 6.2%.

Only two countries in that group averaged less, Panama at 2.1% and El Salvador at 2.4%, and both use the US dollar as their currency. Argentina and Venezuela lack a full series in the World Bank data and Cuba has none, so they are left out.

That makes the claim broadly sound for Spanish- and Portuguese-speaking Latin America outside the dollarised economies, though it is our reading and not a statement Velarde spelled out. Small English-speaking economies such as Belize, the Bahamas and Dominica average lower in the same data, and averages of annual rates are only a rough guide.

Lima Prices Today Sit Above the Target

The statistics office INEI said on Thursday 1 October that Lima prices rose 0.12% in September and 4.55% over 12 months, up from 4.44% in August. Bloomberg Línea counted it as the seventh month above the central bank’s 1% to 3% target range and the highest reading in three years.

INEI chief Gaspar Morán Flores pointed to transport, where vehicle fuels rose 5.2% in the month and taxi fares 0.9%. Across the whole country, INEI put inflation at 4.17% over 12 months.

On Wednesday 7 October the central bank, known as the BCRP, held its policy rate at 4.25% for a 13th straight month, EFE reported through Infobae. The bank said annual inflation rose from 4.4% in August to 4.5% in September and that inflation without food and energy stayed at 4.5%.

That core reading is well above the 2.6% US core rate for September, which the US Bureau of Labor Statistics published on Wednesday 14 October. US headline inflation was 3.7%, so Peru’s long record and its present rate point in different directions.

The bank projects that inflation will return to the target range and settle near 2%, and it warns that El Niño and tension in the Middle East could keep prices higher for longer. Bloomberg Línea reported before the meeting that Velarde expects 4.2% at the end of this year and a return to the range in 2027.

Stable Money, Unstable Politics

Velarde was sworn in on Thursday 24 September for a new term to 2031, Gestión reported, as covered in Peru Keeps Its Central Bank Chief of 20 Years, an Anchor Amid Turmoil. He has used each public platform to argue that central bank independence is why Peru’s economy fared better than its politics would suggest.

At the September event he also said Peru has had 31 prime ministers in 20 years, which he said hurts long-term projects, América TV reported. Our earlier report on the latest rate hold is Peru’s Central Bank Holds Rate at 4.25%.

For the wider map of who sets economic policy, see Who Runs Peru’s Economy, the Key Players in 2026. The sol, mining and political risk are set out in Peru’s Economy: Mining, the Sol, Political Noise and the State of Play.

What It Means for You

For US investors, the century record is part of the case Peru makes for its sol and local bonds, but it is a record of the past. With Lima inflation above target and El Niño a stated risk, it does not guarantee low prices ahead.

For importers of Peruvian copper, gold, blueberries, grapes and fishmeal, Bloomberg Línea notes that weather anomalies have hit transport, crop yields and fishing. For travellers, September’s rise came mainly from fuel and taxi fares, so getting around Lima costs more than a year ago.

What Is Not Known

The reports we read do not show which countries, years and price measure Velarde used, or whether dollarised economies such as Panama count in his comparison. We could not open a central bank transcript of the speech, so his words here come from Infobae and Gestión.

Our World Bank average covers 2001 to 2025 and leaves out Argentina, Cuba and Venezuela, and it does not say which countries Velarde had in mind. Whether Peru’s inflation returns to the 1% to 3% range in 2027 is the bank’s projection, not a fact.

Frequently Asked Questions

Does Peru have the lowest inflation in Latin America this century?

Central bank president Julio Velarde says so, and World Bank data for 2001 to 2025 show Peru averaging 3.0% a year. Among 17 Spanish-, Portuguese- and French-speaking Latin American countries with full data, only dollarised Panama and El Salvador averaged less.

What is Peru’s inflation rate now?

Lima consumer prices rose 4.55% in the 12 months to September, according to the statistics office INEI. The central bank’s target range is 1% to 3%.

How does Peru’s inflation compare with the United States?

US consumer prices rose 3.7% in the 12 months to September and 2.6% without food and energy. Lima’s 4.55% headline and 4.5% core readings are both higher at present.

Who is Julio Velarde?

He is the president of the Banco Central de Reserva del Perú, the central bank, and has held the post for almost 20 years. Gestión reported that he was sworn in on 24 September for a term to 2031.

How did Peru cut the use of dollars in its banks?

Velarde said the bank required prices to be shown in soles as well and set reserve requirements on dollar loans. The dollar share of bank loans fell from 81% in 2000 to 23% today.

Sources: Infobae, 16 October 2026; Gestión, 16 October 2026; INEI press note, 1 October 2026; Bloomberg Línea, 1 October 2026; Infobae (EFE), 7 October 2026; US Bureau of Labor Statistics, 14 October 2026; América TV, 2 September 2026; Gestión, 24 September 2026; Minería & Energía, 15 July 2026; World Bank consumer price inflation series, updated 8 October 2026. Country averages for 2001 to 2025 are Rio Times calculations from the World Bank series.

World.title: Puerto Rico Senate Permit Bill Sent Friday
World.content:
The Capitol of Puerto Rico in San Juan, seat of the Senate and House of Representatives (Photo: Jorge Láscar, CC BY 2.0, via Wikimedia Commons)

PUERTO RICO · PERMITS

Key Facts — The country Puerto Rico is a US territory in the Caribbean whose residents are US citizens, and its own Senate and House make its local laws.

— Why it matters A new planning and permits code would change how land, buildings and parts of the coastline are approved, which touches mainland investors, homeowners and developers.

— Why now The Senate approved the bill on Tuesday 13 October, and the governor’s office received the final text on Friday 16 October at 5:39 p.m.

— What happened The Senate passed a substitute merging Senate Bills 1173 and 1183, and Senate President Thomas Rivera Schatz then sent the text to La Fortaleza by WhatsApp.

— The numbers As drafted, the text repeals 11 laws, amends 30 others and sets fines of up to US$100,000 for false information.

— What it means for you Nothing changes yet, because the House has not voted and no law exists, but permit and coastal rules could shift in the coming weeks.

— Still open Whether the House amends or defeats the bill, and whether Governor Jenniffer González Colón signs or vetoes a final text.

The Senate-approved text of the Puerto Rico permit reform bill reached the governor’s office on Friday 16 October, but it is still a Senate bill and not law. Senate President Thomas Rivera Schatz sent it to La Fortaleza, the governor’s residence and seat of the executive, after Governor Jenniffer González Colón had said that she still lacked the final version with the floor amendments.

The bill rewrites planning and permit rules in a US territory whose residents are US citizens, so it matters to mainland builders, buyers and visitors. It has passed only the Senate, and the House of Representatives still has to act.

What the Puerto Rico Permit Reform Would Change

The Senate approved a substitute bill on Tuesday 13 October that merges Senate Bills 1173 and 1183, El Nuevo Día, Metro Puerto Rico and Sin Comillas reported. Rivera Schatz filed the first of those bills and the governor filed the second.

Rivera Schatz says the text repeals 11 laws and amends 30 others to create one planning and permits code. It keeps the Planning Board, the body that sets land-use rules, and returns some rule-making powers to it.

He lists fixed evaluation deadlines, automatic issuance when the government misses certain deadlines, and fines of up to US$100,000 for false information. He also says the text ends the single permit for future applications and adds use declarations for permitted activities.

The text also writes coastal rules into law, including a 20-metre strip for shoreline monitoring and a six-metre public path beside the maritime-terrestrial zone, Rivera Schatz said. Metro described that zone as public-domain land along the shore.

Metro reported that the text would cut the validity of a boundary survey of that zone from 10 years to five. Rivera Schatz says existing surveys would keep their validity under the conditions in the bill.

The Dispute Over Who Had the Text

Governor González Colón told a press conference on Friday that she still lacked the final text with the amendments introduced on the Senate floor. She said it had reached neither the House nor La Fortaleza.

Rivera Schatz replied on Facebook that the report, the substitute text and the amendments went to Fortaleza officials and House Speaker Carlos “Johnny” Méndez Núñez on 28 September. He named adviser Thaís Reyes, aide Carlos Rivera Justiniano and Secretary of the Governorship Norma Burgos as recipients.

He also posted a text message in which Rivera Justiniano confirmed receiving a document and promised an immediate analysis. La Fortaleza said the final text arrived from Rivera Schatz by WhatsApp at 5:39 p.m. on Friday.

The governor’s legislative team is now comparing the text with both original bills and with private-sector demands for faster permits, La Fortaleza said. Any amendments it identifies would be sent to the Legislative Assembly in due course.

Who Backs the Bill and Who Objects

Luis Javier Hernández Ortiz, the Senate spokesman of the opposition Popular Democratic Party (PPD), said the substitute differs from the text discussed at public hearings. The governing New Progressive Party (PNP) holds the Senate majority, and the PPD delegation voted against the bill.

Hernández Ortiz argues that the bill moves power to the secretary of the Department of Economic Development and Commerce while trimming the permits office, the Planning Board and the municipalities. He also says an amendment adds a bond of at least US$50,000 for anyone trying to halt a project, and independent Senator Joanne Rodríguez Veve, who voted yes, said the bond for challenging permits on projects of US$500,000 or more rose from 1% to 10%, El Nuevo Día reported.

The Puerto Rico Chamber of Commerce was still reviewing the shoreline language when Metro spoke to it on 15 October. The builders’ association welcomed the step but voiced concern over municipal autonomy, and the retailers’ group Centro Unido de Detallistas backs the reform.

The Puerto Rico College of Architects opposes the bill and wants a broader, more participatory process, Sin Comillas said. The Senate says it held five public hearings with agencies, municipal representatives and environmental groups.

What Happens Next in the House

The bill now goes to the House, where Rivera Schatz said it can be amended or defeated. If both chambers agree on a text, it goes to the governor, who can sign it or veto it.

Speaker Méndez Núñez said on Wednesday 14 October that he would wait for the measures approved by the Senate before starting a detailed review, Metro reported. The governor said on Thursday that the House could hold public hearings and that her economic development department would send it comments, El Nuevo Día reported.

What It Means for You

For US readers, Puerto Rico is US soil, so the code would govern building, land use and some coastal access for mainland investors, homeowners and developers. Nothing changes yet, because the House has not passed the bill and no law exists.

Visitors and expats should not expect new beach or building rules this month, and the guides Puerto Rico Explained for Americans, No Presidential Vote and Moving to Puerto Rico 2026 Step by Step cover the wider rules. Anyone with a pending permit or purchase should follow the House debate and ask local counsel what the final text says.

What Is Not Known

The sources reviewed do not show when the House will act or whether Speaker Méndez Núñez will hold public hearings. It is also unknown whether the governor will sign, amend or veto a final text, since her office has only begun its review.

The vote count is reported two ways, with El Nuevo Día and a later Metro story citing 17 votes to eight and three senators not voting, while Metro’s first report described a voice vote. The length is also disputed, since El Nuevo Día and Metro give 868 pages while PPD Senator Josian Santiago put it above 1,000.

The 28 September delivery is Rivera Schatz’s account, which we could not independently confirm, and the effect on permit times and coastal access cannot be measured until a final text exists. Claims by supporters and opponents are projections, not findings.

Frequently Asked Questions

What is the Puerto Rico permit bill?

It is a substitute bill that merges Senate Bills 1173 and 1183 into one planning and permits code. The Senate approved it on Tuesday 13 October 2026.

Has Governor González Colón signed it?

No, because the bill has not passed the House of Representatives. La Fortaleza received the Senate text on Friday 16 October and is comparing it with the original bills.

Why did the governor say she lacked the text?

She said on Friday that the final version with the floor amendments had not reached her. Rivera Schatz says drafts went to her aides on 28 September, while La Fortaleza says the final text arrived on Friday evening.

What does the bill change on the coast?

Its Senate sponsor says it sets a 20-metre shoreline strip and a six-metre public path beside the maritime-terrestrial zone. Metro reported that it would also cut the validity of a boundary survey from 10 years to five.

Who opposes the permit bill?

The opposition Popular Democratic Party voted against it, and the Puerto Rico College of Architects wants a broader process. Business groups are mixed, with some backing it and others still reviewing it.

What happens next?

The House of Representatives can amend or defeat the bill. If both chambers agree on a text, the governor can sign or veto it.

World.title: Costa Rica President Tours CECOT Mega-Prison in El Salvador
World.content:
Costa Rican President Laura Fernández toured El Salvador’s Terrorism Confinement Center (CECOT) today, two days after opening a maximum-security prison in Alajuela modeled on it. Salvadoran officials walked her through the facility and explained how it is run. Fernández landed at San Óscar Arnulfo Romero International Airport, where Salvadoran Foreign Minister Alexandra Hill Tinoco received her.

She then flew by helicopter to the prison in the department of San Vicente, about 74 kilometers (46 miles) from San Salvador, according to Salvadoran media. Defense Minister René Francis Merino Monroy, Justice and Public Security Minister Gustavo Villatoro and CECOT director Belarmino García led the tour. Costa Rica’s Justice and Peace Minister, Gabriel Aguilar, traveled with Fernández.

CECOT has an announced capacity of up to 40,000 inmates. It is surrounded by concrete walls more than 11 meters (36 feet) high and electrified fencing, and it has become the centerpiece of President Nayib Bukele’s crackdown on gangs. Fernández was scheduled to meet Bukele at Casa Presidencial in San Salvador later today to discuss security and regional cooperation, and Salvadoran authorities called a press conference for 3:30 p.m. No agreements between the two governments had been announced as of Friday afternoon.

Before the trip, Fernández said she wanted to study CECOT’s operating model in depth, beyond its physical design. At the opening of Costa Rica’s new prison, she thanked Bukele for El Salvador’s support in the fight against organized crime. The High Containment Center Against Organized Crime (CACCO) opened Wednesday in the La Reforma prison complex in San Rafael de Alajuela. It is designed to hold 5,100 high-profile inmates in five modules of 1,020 each. Aguilar has said it will reach full occupancy in December.

The construction contract, awarded to Edificar in November 2025, was worth about 16.8 billion colones, roughly $33 million. The prison opens as Costa Rica’s inmate population sits at a record 21,173. The opening has drawn legal and political pushback. An association representing prisoners and their families has filed an appeal with the Constitutional Chamber seeking to halt transfers to the facility, arguing it poses health and safety risks to inmates.

At the inauguration, Fernández accused magistrates, prosecutors and judges of siding with criminals, deepening a dispute between the executive branch and the judiciary. Magistrates invited to the ceremony did not attend. Supporters of El Salvador’s model credit it with a steep drop in homicides, while human rights groups have criticized mass detentions and conditions inside its prisons. Costa Rica recorded 873 homicides in 2025, a rate of 16.7 per 100,000 inhabitants, according to the Judicial Investigation Agency (OIJ).

World.title: Flood alert issued across Belize as heavy rainfall threatens rivers and low-lying areas; 2 – 4 inches of rain possible over some areas
World.content:
Flood alert issued across Belize as heavy rainfall threatens rivers and low-lying areas; 2 – 4 inches of rain possible over some areas

By Hugh O’Brien: A flood alert across Belize has been issued as additional rainfall is expected to affect the country over the weekend.

According to the National Meteorological Service (NMS) in the Ministry of Sustainable Development and Climate Change, rainfall forecasts of “2 – 4 inches are possible over portions of Belize during the next four days”.

Residents in low-lying, flood-prone and riverside communities especially are advised to remain alert and to closely monitor official weather and flood updates as conditions may change rapidly.

During periods of heavy rainfall, the NMS advises caution “near rivers, streams, low-level crossings and other flood-prone areas” and residents are advised “to not attempt to cross flooded roads or waterways”.

According to the NMS, “several rivers are currently at normal or below-normal levels”. However, additional rainfall could cause smaller streams and tributaries to rise quickly, while larger river systems may respond more gradually as rainfall accumulates. Particular attention is being urged for rivers that are already elevated or approaching bankfull levels.

In its latest weather forecast, the NMS reported that in the north, rivers are near or below normal. In the west, the Mopan River, in particular, has shown a moderate increase in water level, but remain near or below normal. The Belize River is “above normal levels at More Tomorrow” but further downstream toward the coast, and at the Crooked Tree Lagoon, levels are below normal.

In the south, the Sittee River is rising toward bankfull levels and is a cause for concern for increased flooding. The Gales Point Lagoon, Moho River, Temash River and Sarstoon are rising above normal levels

Despite the current conditions in the nation’s rivers, the NMS warns that further rainfall could lead to rapid changes, particularly in smaller waterways and areas that are already vulnerable to flooding.

The NMS says it will continue to monitor rainfall and river conditions and that the flood outlook may be updated if forecast conditions or field observations change.

World.title: Police seek public’s help to identify two-year-old girl found in Belize City
World.content:
Police seek public’s help to identify two-year-old girl found in Belize City

UPDATE: The 2-year-old girl has been reunited with her parents.

By Breaking Belize News Staff: The Belize Police Department is appealing to the public for assistance in identifying a two-year-old girl who was found on Carissa Street in Belama Phase Two, Belize City, on Friday, October 16, 2026.

Crime Stoppers Belize has circulated a photograph of the child in hopes that someone will recognize her and help authorities establish her identity and locate her family.

Police have not yet disclosed the circumstances under which the child was found or whether any parent or guardian has come forward.

Anyone who recognizes the child or has information that could assist police is urged to call 615-5179, contact Crime Stoppers anonymously at 922, use the P3 Tips app, or visit the nearest police station.

The Belize Police Department confirms that information submitted through Crime Stoppers can be provided anonymously.

World.title: Man accused of torching Hotchandani family’s $485,000 vehicles still without attorney as arson case heads to High Court
World.content:
Man accused of torching Hotchandani family’s $485,000 vehicles still without attorney as arson case heads to High Court

By Breaking Belize News Staff: Nearly two years after three luxury vehicles belonging to businessman Bob Hotchandani and his son were destroyed in a suspected arson attack, the man accused of setting them ablaze is still without an attorney as his case moves toward trial in the High Court.

Twenty-four-year-old Manuel Anthony Moralez appeared unrepresented before Justice Candace Nanton on Friday for a case management conference involving three counts of arson.

When questioned about legal representation, Moralez told the court that he intended to secure an attorney and would try his best to do so if granted additional time.

Justice Nanton agreed to adjourn the matter until March 15, 2027, giving Moralez approximately five months to obtain legal representation. However, she warned that if he remains unrepresented by then, the court will have to proceed with setting a trial date.

Moralez, a construction worker from Sandhill Village, was charged with three counts of arson in December 2024 following a fire that destroyed three vehicles parked outside the Hotchandani family residence on Barrack Road in Belize City.

The vehicles included a 2022 Cadillac Escalade valued at $250,000 and a 2023 Audi Q7 valued at $150,000, both belonging to 75-year-old businessman Bob Hotchandani. A Chevrolet Silverado pickup truck valued at $85,000, belonging to his son, Sunjay Hotchandani, was also destroyed.

According to earlier reporting by 7News, police said three men arrived at the property by boat shortly before 5:00 a.m. on December 22, 2024, poured a flammable substance on the vehicles and set them on fire before escaping by boat.

Surveillance cameras reportedly captured the attack, and police subsequently identified Moralez as one of the alleged perpetrators.

At his initial arraignment, prosecutors opposed bail, citing the substantial value of the destroyed vehicles, the surveillance evidence and concerns that Moralez could interfere with the investigation or face retaliation from other persons allegedly involved. He was subsequently remanded to the Belize Central Prison.

The case has since been committed to the High Court for trial, but proceedings remain stalled while Moralez attempts to secure legal representation.

Moralez’s next court appearance is scheduled for March 15, 2027.

World.title: BTB leads Belizean tour operators to FCCA Cruise Conference
World.content:
BTB leads Belizean tour operators to FCCA Cruise Conference

By Breaking Belize News Staff (HP): The Belize Tourism Board led a delegation of Belizean tour operators to the Florida Caribbean Cruise Association’s 32nd Annual Cruise Conference, held October 12 to 16 in San Juan, Puerto Rico.

The conference is one of the region’s largest cruise tourism events, bringing together more than 700 delegates, including cruise line executives, destination leaders and government representatives from across the Caribbean and the Americas.

Belizean operators met one on one with cruise line executives to showcase their tours and explore opportunities to secure direct contracts for the upcoming cruise season.

The delegation also connected with tour operators from across the region to share best practices and discuss ways to improve the cruise guest experience.

The BTB says it remains committed to supporting local tour operators and strengthening Belize’s position as a competitive, premier cruise destination. It thanked the participating operators for representing Belize with professionalism and pride.

World.title: Two years without Court-ordered psychiatric reviews: Shedrack White’s murder case remains in limbo
World.content:
Two years without Court-ordered psychiatric reviews: Shedrack White’s murder case remains in limbo

By Breaking Belize News Staff: The High Court is still grappling with the case of Shedrack White, a man accused of murder who was declared mentally unfit to stand trial more than two years ago, after it emerged that court-ordered psychiatric evaluations were never conducted as required.

White appeared before Justice Candace Nanton on Friday, represented by attorney Norman Rodriguez, as the court sought to determine his current mental fitness and whether he should remain at the Belize Central Prison or be placed elsewhere.

In February 2024, Justice Nanton ruled that White was unfit to stand trial after he was diagnosed with schizophrenia. The court ordered that he receive appropriate treatment at the Kolbe Foundation and undergo psychiatric evaluations every six months, with the results submitted to the court.

However, Justice Nanton noted on Friday that those periodic reviews had not been carried out as ordered, raising questions about why the court’s instructions were not followed.

Although a psychiatric assessment was conducted in June 2026, the judge found it insufficient because it failed to address whether White was currently fit to enter a plea or stand trial.

A further evaluation has now been ordered, with the psychiatrist given until October 20 to complete the assessment and until October 27 for the report to be filed with the court.

Justice Nanton acknowledged that several difficult questions remain, particularly if White continues to be found unfit to stand trial. These include whether he should remain at the Belize Central Prison, be transferred to another suitable facility or be released into the care of his family.

During an earlier hearing in September, White’s sister, Priscilla White, expressed willingness to accommodate him at the family home and ensure he receives his medication. However, the court must also consider his safety, access to treatment and any potential risk to the public.

White is accused of the July 29, 2020 murder of William Rubio, who was fatally stabbed during an altercation near the Pound Yard Bridge in Belize City.

During the original competency proceedings in 2024, government psychiatrist Dr. Alejandro Matus testified that White had undergone four psychiatric assessments and was diagnosed with schizophrenia. The doctor indicated that White would require lifelong treatment and was unlikely to become fit to stand trial.

Justice Nanton has ordered Crown Counsel Glenfield Dennison to file the prosecution’s written submissions by November 5, while the defense must file its submissions by November 12.

The matter has been adjourned to November 16, 2026, when the court is expected to consider the psychiatric findings and arguments from both sides before determining the way forward.

White has not been convicted of Rubio’s murder, and his fitness to stand trial remains unresolved.

World.title: Jamie Young’s murder trial pushed to 2027 as Court offers sentencing indication following failed plea talks
World.content:
Jamie Young’s murder trial pushed to 2027 as Court offers sentencing indication following failed plea talks

By Breaking Belize News Staff: The murder trial of Jamie Caesar Young, accused of fatally shooting his former girlfriend’s new partner during a highway pursuit in 2024, has been pushed back to 2027 after plea discussions between the defense and prosecution failed to produce an agreement.

Young appeared before High Court Justice Candace Nanton on Friday, where his attorney, Dr. Lynden Jones, informed the court that discussions with the Crown had not reached a successful conclusion and that the matter would therefore proceed to trial.

However, with the court’s calendar already fully booked for the remainder of 2026, Justice Nanton informed the parties that a new trial date would have to be scheduled for next year.

In an unusual development, Justice Nanton invited the defense to consider a Maximum Sentence Indication (MSI), a procedure through which the court would indicate the maximum sentence Young could face if he entered a guilty plea under the circumstances presented. Jones accepted the court’s offer on his client’s behalf.

The defense has been ordered to file its submissions and agreed facts of the case by 4:00 p.m. on Monday, October 19. Justice Nanton is expected to deliver the sentencing indication at 1:00 p.m. on Friday, October 23.

The judge made clear that Young is not obligated to accept the indication and that declining it would not prejudice his right to proceed to trial.

Young is charged with the March 16, 2024 murder of 30-year-old Damion Dominique Baptist, a bus driver and former Belize Defence Force soldier from Burrell Boom Village.

According to earlier reports by Breaking Belize News, Baptist was driving a red Ford Fusion along the Philip Goldson Highway with Young’s former girlfriend, Laneedrah Dawson, when Young allegedly pursued them in a grey pickup truck.

Investigators allege that Young repeatedly pulled alongside their vehicle and opened fire. Baptist was eventually struck in the head near Our Lady of the Way RC School in Ladyville, causing him to lose control of the vehicle and crash into a lamppost. He was pronounced dead after being transported to the Karl Heusner Memorial Hospital.

Young subsequently surrendered to police and was charged with murder and aggravated assault against Dawson.

During pre-trial proceedings in May, prosecutors indicated that they intended to rely on surveillance footage, photographs and material allegedly extracted from a phone, while the defense disclosed plans to call an alibi witness.

The trial has since suffered several postponements, including an October 5 adjournment after Jones reportedly fell ill and another postponement on Thursday.

The latest development leaves open the possibility of resolving the case without a trial, depending on the sentencing indication and Young’s decision. If no agreement is reached, the murder trial will proceed in 2027.

World.title: Police recover stolen SUV following Burrell Boom home invasion; two detained
World.content:
Police recover stolen SUV following Burrell Boom home invasion; two detained

By Breaking Belize News Staff: Police have recovered a stolen Toyota SUV and detained two persons of interest following an aggravated burglary in Burrell Boom Village, Belize District, early Wednesday morning.

Assistant Superintendent of Police Stacy Smith said the incident occurred around 3:30 a.m. on October 14, when a resident was awakened by noises inside his home. Upon investigating, he was confronted and assaulted by an intruder before being restrained.

The victim reportedly observed three other men inside the residence. The assailants ransacked the property and escaped with an undisclosed amount of cash, jewellery, a cellphone and his Toyota SUV.

Smith said police subsequently issued an alert for the stolen vehicle, which was spotted by officers patrolling Santa Familia Village in the Cayo District. A pursuit followed, during which the occupants abandoned the SUV and fled.

The vehicle was recovered and processed for forensic evidence, including fingerprints, as investigators worked to identify those responsible.

Smith confirmed that two persons of interest have been detained, while another individual is being sought in connection with the burglary.

The stolen vehicle was previously reported to be a burgundy 2017 Toyota Rush taken from a residence in Burrell Boom.

Police investigations continue.

World.title: Fernando Jones, Esau Perez shot dead at wake in Cotton Tree Village; police suspect ongoing feud
World.content:
Fernando Jones, Esau Perez shot dead at wake in Cotton Tree Village; police suspect ongoing feud

By Breaking Belize News Staff: Police are investigating a double murder in Cotton Tree Village, Cayo District, where 27-year-old Fernando Jones and 21-year-old Esau Perez were shot and killed early Friday morning following a wake.

According to Assistant Superintendent of Police Stacy Smith, officers on patrol heard gunshots at approximately 3:57 a.m. and responded to the area, where they discovered both men with apparent gunshot wounds.

Investigators believe Jones was the intended target. Smith explained that Jones was leaving the wake when an armed man emerged and fired several shots at him. As the gunman fled, he also fired in the direction of Perez, fatally wounding him.

Smith said investigators believe the shooting is connected to an ongoing dispute between rival factions operating in the village. Two persons of interest have been detained as investigations continue.

Police are also preparing for possible retaliation. Smith confirmed that operational efforts in the village have been adjusted, particularly with another wake or gathering reportedly scheduled for Friday night.

She acknowledged that police had already stationed a patrol in Cotton Tree because of previous violent incidents but revealed that Commissioner of Police Dr. Richard Rosado identified a lapse in patrol operations on the night of the murders.

Smith said corrective action would be taken and those responsible for the lapse would be held accountable.

Cotton Tree has experienced previous incidents of gun violence, including a double murder in 2024 and another fatal shooting in August 2026. However, police have not established any connection between those incidents and Friday’s killings.

World.title: Market Bag: Farmers hopeful that rains will cool prices
World.content:
KINGSTON, Jamaica — Farmers in Mandeville are optimistic that recent rainfall will boost agricultural production and bring much-needed relief to consumers, as produce prices remain high amid an extended period of drought.

During this week’s visit to the Mandeville Market, lettuce was among the most expensive items, selling for $1,400 per pound. Sweet peppers were priced at $600 per pound, while tomatoes and carrots were each selling for $500 per pound.

Sweet potatoes were going for $450 per pound, escallion for $400 per pound and onions and Irish potatoes for $300 per pound. Scotch bonnet peppers were being sold for $200 per bag.

Despite the high prices, farmers told Market Bag host Carlysia Ramdeen that improving weather conditions have renewed hopes for increased production and a possible reduction in prices in the coming weeks.

One farmer, who only identified himself as ‘Stone’, explained that the return of rainfall, coupled with cooler temperatures, is encouraging more farmers to resume planting.

“Now everybody is going to go out and plant because we getting back little rain, the temperature are dropping, so more farmers are going out and planting now, so prices gonna come down for a while,” Stone shared.

However, he cautioned that any relief could be short-lived, noting that excessive rainfall could also disrupt production and drive prices higher.

“That vary on how the weather keep up. If we get too much rain, production is going to go down, so that is going to surge the prices,” he added.

Fellow farmer Orando White echoed those sentiments, noting that it remains too early to determine how the recent rainfall would affect produce prices.

“Even if there is a price decrease, I believe that it will be stable enough where customers and sellers likewise and farmers can be happy at the same time,” White said.

Catch the latest episode of Market Bag on all Jamaica Observer digital platforms.

World.title: ‘Deeply troubling’: JTA alarmed as 15 Kingston High teachers get termination letters
World.content:
LaSonja Harrison, JTA President

More than a dozen teachers at Kingston High School have been issued termination letters by the institution’s Board of Management, a move described by Jamaica Teachers’ Association (JTA) president La Sonja Harrison as “deeply troubling” and “extremely egregious”.

Observer Online understands that 15 teachers, some of whom have been employed at the institution for more than a year, received the letters following a recent board meeting. The letters were signed by the chairman of the school board, Carlton Samuels and Acting Principal Sashauna Gordon.

Samuels told Observer Online that the separations were based on assessments and the performance of the teachers.

“We had a situation where we did have some separations based on assessments, outcomes, and performance, and it’s not fully completed yet. That’s as much as I can say right now,” he said.

However, the school’s principal, Jermaine Loutin, described the affected educators as excellent teachers who deserved permanent appointments, also pointing to the performance of one teacher whose subject area, he said, recorded a 100 per cent pass rate over the past three years.

Loutin, who is currently on vacation leave, said he had recommended that approximately 32 teachers be granted permanent appointments at the board’s last meeting in June. He said he subsequently learnt that the board had met and issued termination letters to some teachers.

“Most of these teachers, when I say most, 99 per cent of them are excellent teachers who are due their permanent appointment,” Loutin said. “I have seen some of the letters that teachers have sent to me, but I would have expressed to them that I have nothing to do with this.

“My recommendation for them was for them to be made permanent, so I cannot say why the board would have made that decision,” the principal said.

He further alleged an ongoing challenge of recommendations submitted by the principal to the board being disregarded.

“I cannot say why the board would have made that decision. But I know that the matter has been reported to the JTA, and the matter has also been reported to the Ministry of Education, and they are conducting their investigation,” Loutin shared.

Termination letters seen by Observer Online were all dated October 6, 2026 and stated that the teachers’ employment would end on October 21.

The letters, issued by the school’s Board of Management, said the decision followed a review of the teachers’ personnel file, appraisal records, attendance and punctuality, as well as assessment outcomes for classes taught between December 2025 and June 2026.

The board said the school’s administration would discuss arrangements for ending the teachers’ employment, including outstanding compensation, applicable benefits and the return of school property.

JTA president La Sonja Harrison said the association became aware of the matter last Friday after the affected teachers lodged complaints with its South-East Regional Office.

She said the association has since raised the issue at its monthly meeting with the Ministry of Education and is awaiting the outcome of a meeting between the ministry and the school’s board chairman scheduled for next Wednesday.

“To our understanding, the teachers would have been engaged for more than a year, and so, having received the letter, the situation is very concerning, egregious to our mind in some case, but as we said, we are awaiting to see what are the outcomes, deliberations, talks, what is coming out of those conversations with the board, and then the association will take it further,” she said.

“It is a very deeply troubling matter, extremely egregious if you ask me, but we are awaiting since the ministry assured us that they will be having a meeting on Wednesday concerning the same,” she continued.

The JTA president further pointed to provisions under the Code of Regulations for Teachers governing the termination of teachers’ services.

“Just as when persons complain that the teachers leave and should give at least three months’ notice. The teachers should receive notice, and the teachers have to receive notice at a particular time because the code tells you that the teacher is engaged and, over a period of a year, three terms, we would carry out the necessary supervisory matters and then engage in an appraisal and terming before the end of the third term, if it is that the school will continue with the services of the teacher or not,” Harrison said.

Minister of Education and Youth Senator Dana Morris Dixon told Observer Online that she had been informed of the matter and has since instructed Permanent Secretary Dr Kasan Troupe to investigate the development.

She said an update will be provided after receiving the investigation report.

World.title: JCF will not be intimidated, Blake declares after deadly Sligoville attack
World.content:
Police Commissioner Dr Kevin Blake

ST CATHERINE, Jamaica — Commissioner of Police Dr Kevin Blake has vowed that the Jamaica Constabulary Force (JCF) will not retreat in its fight against criminal gangs following Friday morning’s deadly gun attack on police personnel in Sligoville, St Catherine, which left one officer dead and another critically injured.

In a strongly worded statement, Blake condemned the attack, declaring that the police would intensify their efforts to dismantle criminal networks responsible for violence across the island.

“Let there be no misunderstanding. The Jamaica Constabulary Force will not be intimidated. We will not retreat and we will not relent,” Blake declared.

“Those responsible and the criminal networks that enable them will be pursued, dismantled and be brought to justice. There can be no community ceded to gunmen, no safe haven for gangs, no territory beyond the reach of the law,” he added.

The deceased officer has been identified as Corporal Trevoy Shaw, who was attached to the JCF’s Special Operations unit.

Another policeman, who sustained gunshot wounds to the head, is undergoing surgery, while several other police personnel and a young girl were also injured during the confrontation.

The girl is reportedly in serious but stable condition.

READ: UPDATE: Two men killed after gun battle with police in Sligoville

Reports are that about 5:15 am, a team from the JCF’s Special Operations unit was conducting an operation in the Five Miles area of Sligoville in search of wanted men.

The officers were reportedly clearing a building on a premises when they came under heavy gunfire from two men who had barricaded themselves inside a house with other occupants.

Both gunmen were subsequently killed during the confrontation.

According to Blake, the officers were pursuing a high-risk target linked to violent crime when they came under sustained gunfire.

“This tragedy lays bare the brutal conditions our officers confront daily, pursuing the most violent elements in our society, so that Jamaicans can live without fear,” the commissioner said.

“We expect every officer we deploy to return home safely. Today, that expectation was shattered,” he added.

Blake also expressed condolences to the family of the fallen corporal and pledged the force’s support for the injured officer and his relatives.

“We mourn with the family of our fallen colleague and stand firmly with the family of our injured member,” he said.

Despite the tragedy, the police commissioner maintained that the JCF remains resolute in its efforts to confront violent criminals.

“Our resolve is undiminished, our duty unchanged. We grieve, but we will act,” Blake declared.

World.title: Court injunction blocks PNP bid to take control of Clarendon Municipal Corporation
World.content:
CLARENDON, Jamaica — An interim injunction has blocked the People’s National Party’s (PNP) bid to take control of the Clarendon Municipal Corporation, following a Supreme Court order presented during a special meeting of the council on Friday.

The court order barred the council from debating or voting on key agenda items relating to the proposed removal of Mayor Joel Williams and Deputy Mayor Clivalee Mundle.

The development comes amid political tensions at the municipal corporation following the announcement by Councillor for the May Pen North Division, Tanya-Lee Williams that she intends to leave the Jamaica Labour Party (JLP) and join the PNP.

Williams reportedly attempted to cross the floor during Thursday’s sitting of the municipal corporation. However, the move was ruled inadmissible after she failed to follow the correct procedure under the council’s standing orders, resulting in the adjournment of the meeting.

In a statement on Thursday, the JLP said it had taken note of Williams’ announcement but had not received a formal resignation letter from the councillor.

The party said processes had been activated to facilitate her expulsion.

READ: JLP moves to expel councillor after announced defection to PNP

World.title: No final for JC as ISSA upholds Walker Cup ban
World.content:
Jamone Lyle (second right) and his Jamaica College teammates celebrate a goal in their Walker Cup semi-final against Mona High on Saturday, October 10, 2026. (Photo: Garfield Robinson)

KINGSTON, Jamaica — The Inter-Secondary Schools Sports Association (ISSA) has upheld its ban on Jamaica College (JC), rejecting the school’s appeal after it was removed from the Walker Cup for using an ineligible player.

ISSA imposed the sanctions over the eligibility of footballer Jamone Lyle on October 13, days before the Walker Cup final set for Friday, October 16.

The decision was shared via press release Friday morning, with ISSA indicating the Executive Committee has upheld all decisions made by the disciplinary committee.

JC Board of Management Chairman Lance Hylton said the appeal had been lodged within 24 hours of the ruling, describing the penalties as “unsupportable, extreme and excessive”.

READ: JC appeals ISSA sanctions over Jamone Lyle, says procedure was unfair

The sanctions followed a ruling that JC fielded an ineligible player after Lyle was found to have a professional contract with Waterhouse Football Club, making him ineligible for schoolboy football under ISSA regulations.

JC was subsequently removed from the Walker Cup, banned from next year’s competition and ordered to forfeit its Manning Cup second-round match against St Catherine, which it had won 3-2. The game result was reversed to a 3-0 victory for St Catherine.

The decision also paved the way for Kingston College (KC) to face Mona High in Friday’s Walker Cup final, after Mona lost to JC in the semi-final on penalties.

World.title: UPDATE: Two men killed after gun battle with police in Sligoville
World.content:
ST CATHERINE, Jamaica — The two men who barricaded themselves inside a house with other occupants and engaged policemen in a gun battle in Sligoville, St Catherine, on Friday have been killed.

The morning shoot-out left one policeman dead and several other police personnel and a young girl injured.

The deceased officer has been identified as Corporal Trevoy Shaw, who was attached to the Jamaica Constabulary Force’s (JCF) Special Operations unit.

Another policeman, who sustained gunshot wounds to the head, is undergoing surgery. The injured girl is reported to be in serious but stable condition.

The confrontation began about 5:15 am when a team from the JCF’s Special Operations unit carried out an operation in the Five Miles area of Sligoville in search of wanted men.

The cops were reportedly clearing a building on a premises when they came under gunfire from the two men, who had barricaded themselves inside the house with other occupants.

A strong police presence remains in the area as investigations continue.

READ: Cop killed, others injured in Sligoville gun battle

— Llewellyn Wynter

World.title: Cop killed, others injured in Sligoville gun battle
World.content:
ST CATHERINE, Jamaica — An ongoing gun battle in Sligoville, St Catherine, has left several cops injured and at least one lawman killed, according to reports reaching Observer Online.

The Observer understands that the incident began about 5:15 am on Friday when a team from the Jamaica Constabulary Force’s (JCF) Special Operations unit was conducting an operation in the Five Miles area of Sligoville in search of wanted men.

The cops were reportedly clearing a building on a premises when they came under gunfire from two men who had barricaded themselves inside the house among other occupants.

During the exchange, a young girl who was inside the building reportedly sustained gunshot injuries. It is understood that she managed to escape from the house and was taken to hospital by a police team.

Sources described her condition as serious but stable.

Members of the JCF’s SWAT Team, Area 5 Area Fugitive Apprehension Team (AFAT), the Jamaica Defence Force (JDF) and other police personnel are on the scene as the operation continues.

More information to come.

— Llewellyn Wynter

World.title: DOMESTIC DISPUTE TURNS FATAL
World.content:
Nesta Anderson, a window maker and disc jockey who reportedly committed suicide after stabbing his wife who was taken hospital where she is said to be battling for life.

SAVANNA-LA-MAR, Westmoreland — The usually quiet community of New Market Oval in Savanna- la-Mar has been left in shock following a violent family dispute that left a nurse battling for life in hospital and her husband dead.

The husband, Nesta Anderson, a window maker and disc jockey, was from a neighbouring community. Police report that the couple had been involved in a dispute at their home when the woman was allegedly stabbed by Anderson.

Following the attack, Anderson used a ratchet knife to inflict stab wounds to his abdomen about 10:30 am Thursday.

He was rushed to hospital where he was pronounced dead. The Jamaica Observer was told that the couple, who had been together for more than a decade, has three young children.

Unconfirmed reports suggest the children witnessed the incident. When the Observer visited the community, police were processing the scene, while residents shied away from speaking publicly about the matter.

President of the Cooke Street Benevolent Society Bishop O’Neil Russell said he spoke with Anderson just a few days ago and that the incident came as a complete shock as the family was known to be quiet.

“We had a conversation because, you know, there were some things that the benevolent society was supposed to do for him.

We are always in constant dialogue, but he had not shown any sign of depression. It is so shocking. It comes as a shock to see really what took place,” stated Russell.

Councillor Julian Chang (Jamaica Labour Party, Savanna-la-Mar Division), who visited the scene, expressed sadness over the tragedy.

“It’s not anything to rejoice over. We all have issues, and we all have problems. We all go through things,” stated Chang.

She noted that the community, which was devastated by Hurricane Melissa last October, is already under stress and attempting to rebuild.

“We understand the constraints, but you know, we have to deal with our problems better than this, instead of taking our own lives or taking the lives of others,” stated Chang, who joined Russell in calling on people having problems to seek help.

Domestic violence, it can affect anyone regardless of our income, education, or social status. It stretches across all socio-economic backgrounds. We just have to understand that it is right in our midst and we should not be ashamed of it.

We should seek help. And I implore the persons in the Savanna-la-Mar Division, or anywhere for that matter in Jamaica, to seek help because I’m sure there are telltale signs even before it occurs,” Chang said.

She also emphasised the need for community sensitisation to stop judging victims and instead offer support, “because we all deserve to be safe in our own homes”.

World.title: EU leaders clash over migration, Ukraine and budget in Brussels — but delay big decisions
World.content:
Speaking to journalists during a packed news conference, Ukraine’s wartime leader urged his European counterparts to come up with a financial plan or risk facing an unprecedented migration crisis with “20 million Ukrainians” fleeing to Europe.

“The war will cost €155 billion next year. And we need at least €70 billion more from you — for defense, for weapons, and for our resilience,” Zelenskyy said. “This is a realistic amount. And I ask you to find this support. It will help us hold Russia back.”

But two diplomats told POLITICO that capitals would continue exploring a range of options to meet Kyiv’s needs, including a potential further loan from the EU.

Luc Frieden and Emmanuel Macron speak ahead of a round table during the EU summit in Brussels on Oct. 15, 2026. | Ludovic Marin/AFP via Getty Images

A debate over whether to mobilize some €300 billion in Russian frozen assets to help Ukraine is a case in point. Nearly a year after EU leaders rejected using the assets amid objections from Belgium, France and Italy, several countries have asked for the option to be revisited, and top EU diplomat Kaja Kallas had said frozen assets would be on the table when leaders met in Brussels.

But after hours of talks about Ukraine, “nothing has changed,” said Swedish Prime Minister Ulf Kristersson. “The money is not lost but in my belief nothing has happened since we had the discussion last time.”

“In the short term, money to support Ukraine must come from other sources than the frozen assets,” he concluded.

World.title: EU faces growing pressure to plug Ukraine’s Starlink gap
World.content:
"It is unacceptable for Ukraine’s defense — and therefore Europe’s security — to depend on the goodwill of a single American billionaire or on Donald Trump’s decisions," French centrist Member of the European Parliament Christophe Grudler told POLITICO.

Ahead of Thursday's high-level meeting, European lawmakers had been calling on the EU executive to fast-track Kyiv's access to satellite capabilities already pooled under the bloc’s Govsatcom program — which gives participating governments secure communications capabilities.

Negotiations between the EU executive and Ukraine over this access have been ongoing since March, with no breakthrough. Norway and Iceland secured such an agreement earlier this year.

"What I don’t understand is why the European Commission and the Member States have not done everything possible to quickly reach an agreement that would allow Ukraine to benefit from it," added Christophe Grudler, who wrote to EU leaders.

He also called on them to speed up work on IRIS² — the EU’s in-house, planned satellite network and full-fledged match to Starlink, which is only expected to come online in 2030.

Commission spokesperson Thomas Regnier confirmed in a statement that it is "currently in talks with Ukraine to fully associate" the country with the EU's Govsatcom program. "The war in Ukraine shows that our security also depends on space. And the EU has been doing quite a lot. We are ready to support Ukraine where we can support Ukraine," he added.

World.title: 21 things we learned at the EU leaders’ summit
World.content:
1) Energy stole the show right out of the gate

The summit’s first major clash came Thursday morning, with EU leaders split over whether to delay ETS2, the bloc’s second phase of carbon pricing, to address high energy prices, triggering a three-hour-long standoff.

Italy and Greece joined the Visegrád Four — Czechia, Hungary, Poland and Slovakia — in calling for a delay, a push rejected by the majority of countries.

The debate dragged on, delaying lunch (spare a thought for our hungry leaders!) and leading to the cancellation of a press conference on Thursday night.

2) Budget negotiations are a marathon…

Negotiations on the bloc’s next long-term budget were expected to be one of the summit’s most contentious topics. But they were a nothingburger, with most leaders repeating positions they have held for months. The summit brought them no closer to a breakthrough.

Many countries, of course, want a smaller budget, with Swedish Prime Minister Ulf Kristersson telling reporters that his country is “not an ATM for the EU.”

Belgian Prime Minister Bart De Wever, meanwhile, said he had no choice but to be frugal at the European level, arguing he is used to tightening his belt at home because his wife is Dutch. Think of Bart next time your Dutch friends ask you to pay them back for that coffee.

World.title: In Europe’s tech capital, Irish labor unions are booming amid AI-driven layoffs
World.content:
Ireland's lucrative tech sector has been rattled by waves of AI-driven layoffs — and the country's fledgling tech union has seen an exponential spike in sign-ups from workers who are worried about their future.

There’s an “awakening” happening right now among workers in Ireland’s tech sector, and a growing “awareness that they’re not bulletproof,” said Sinéad Gibney, a social democrat lawmaker who previously worked for Google.

“I do think what we will see is that parts of roles will be automated, which means that people will be competing more heavily for the same roles," she said. "They won't have the same labor power and therefore we're going to see a drop in quality of work, we're going to see more zero-hour contracts, in more places than we already see it.”

The labor movement brewing in Ireland, where many of the world's tech giants have their EU bases, is part of a wider trend among tech workers globally, who have seen their work disrupted by rapidly evolving AI.

Rise in layoffs

Ireland’s dedicated union for tech workers, the Digital and Techworker Alliance (DATA), has seen a five-fold increase in membership since it was first founded in 2023.

In its first year and a half of existence, membership hovered around 270 people. In the past year-and-a-half, it's jumped to more than 1,350 members, DATA organizer John Bohan told POLITICO. He added that this number tends to spike around layoffs and other actions.

World.title: Scottish government set to drop opposition to new oil and gas fields
World.content:
The Scottish government — led by the SNP since 2007 — released a draft energy strategy in 2023 which set out its “presumption against” new oil and gas fields in the North Sea.

That draft strategy is “out of date,” one senior Scottish government official said. They said a new strategy, expected by the summer, will not contain this wording. A second person with knowledge of the policy said the new strategy will “reflect the world as it is.”

The shift in policy comes with the U.K. government widely expected to give the go-ahead to the Jackdaw gas field next week.

While the Scottish government has little power over the granting of new licenses for projects such as Jackdaw or the Rosebank oil field — where a decision is expected to come separately and at a later date — it has an important symbolic role, and can apply pressure to the U.K. government to approve licenses.

SNP politicians at the party’s conference in Aberdeen privately admitted the stance on Jackdaw has hurt the party electorally.

The party passed a resolution at its conference Friday which stated that the “utilisation of domestic production” of oil and gas is “clearly preferable to importation”. This was seen as a further softening of the position of the SNP — which governed in a quasi-coalition with the anti-exploration Scottish Greens until as recently as 2004.

World.title: Zelenskyy warns 20M Ukrainians could flee to Europe if Russia wins war
World.content:
The stark warning comes as Kyiv heads into a brutal winter and faces a cash crunch.

BRUSSELS — Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy warned Friday that as many as 20 million Ukrainians could be forced to flee to Europe if his country falls to Russia.

“Russia is killing us,” Zelenskyy told reporters at a press conference on Friday during a summit of European Union leaders, adding Ukrainians were being “pushed” out of their country. “They [Russia] don’t want to stop.”

In the early days of Russia’s full-scale invasion, millions of Ukrainians fled their homes in Europe’s fastest and largest refugee crisis since World War II. Today, over 4 million Ukrainians live in EU countries under temporary protection status, with the largest populations in Germany, Poland and Czechia, according to Eurostat.

Zelenskyy’s stark warning comes as Ukraine heads into a brutal fifth wartime winter under Russian bombardment. Kyiv faces a budget shortfall of $30 to $35 million next year, according to projections from the International Monetary Fund — even accounting for a €90 billion loan Brussels agreed to provide last year.

The Ukrainian president traveled to Brussels to meet with European leaders and shore up financial support for his embattled country. While the EU is Ukraine’s staunchest backer, the bloc’s list of priorities is stacked with rising energy costs, looming elections, geopolitical crises and an impasse over its €2 trillion budget.

World.title: Denmark, Italy, Poland urge EU leaders to harden stance on irregular migration
World.content:
The bloc’s 27 leaders were due to discuss migration during a special session on Thursday requested by Meloni and Frederiksen following a tense back-and-forth with Spanish Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez in June.

Tensions have risen further after Spain’s Ceuta exclave was overwhelmed by migrants during the summer and as far-right parties have made gains around the bloc.

The draft also “calls the Commission to explore [a] possible consultation mechanism to encourage coordination on national measures potentially affecting other Member States while respecting national competencies.”

While the last phrase does not name any one country, Sánchez has clashed with Meloni over his handling of the Ceuta migration crisis as well as Spanish measures to regularize around 1 million migrants.

However, language discussing the impact of migration on social housing was removed from the draft over concerns that it could be perceived as provocative toward Spain.

One of the diplomats — who, like the others, was granted anonymity to discuss confidential information — said the updated draft was unlikely to win unanimous support from all the leaders, but had been proposed to bring the language closer in line with political sentiment and spark debate.

World.title: Spanish opposition leader Feijóo calls for navy to be deployed to Ceuta
World.content:
Feijóo’s calls for a “firm response” are the latest in a wave of criticism of Sánchez’s government after more than 70,000 migrants arrived in the Spanish exclave of Ceuta on the Moroccan border in late July. Migration ministers across the European Union have in recent months repeatedly demanded tough new EU migration policies.

His comments also come after unconfirmed reports that a Moroccan patrol boat remained in Spanish waters off the coast of Ceuta for hours Thursday, which the Spanish Civil Guard has denied. Moroccan warships also allegedly entered Spanish waters in July, though a European Commission spokesperson told Spanish press agency EFE Wednesday that it was “up to the Spanish and Moroccan authorities to clarify the facts.”

Feijóo spent Thursday morning at a summit of the center-right European People’s Party — of which the PP is a member — in Brussels, during which the EPP lashed out at the Spanish government over the Ceuta crisis in its closing statement, according to POLITICO’s Madrid Playbook. Conservatives have said they will implement measures to curb immigration if the government swings to the right after the snap election.

“Europe as a whole must recognize the failure of the Spanish government and exert the necessary pressure to prevent this crisis from becoming entrenched, spreading, or happening again,” Feijóo said in an opinion piece earlier this month.

Tensions over Ceuta and Melilla — which Morocco considers occupied territories — are becoming increasingly strained: A POLITICO poll earlier this week revealed that 58% of respondents believe an armed conflict between Madrid and Rabat is “likely” within the next decade.

In a landmark visit to the exclaves also this week, King Felipe VI said that Ceuta and Melilla were “an inalienable part of the political and national reality that is Spain. The sovereignty and territorial integrity of our country are not negotiable.”

The last time a Spanish head of state visited the territories was in 2007, when former King Juan Carlos I traveled to Ceuta and Melilla amid a diplomatic spat with Morocco.

World.title: No money for Ukraine and EU budget cuts: What could a Le Pen victory mean for the EU?
World.content:
